JISHUMI:v1p622/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p622/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p622/r2.claim: Although safah originally means lightness, in religious usage it became a term of blame applied to disbelievers.
JISHUMI:v1p622/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن اسم السفه، وإن كان في أصل اللغة الخفة، فقد صار في الشرع اسم ذم يجري على الكفار

JISHUMI:v1p645/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p645/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p645/r10.claim: Without transmitted reports, Abu Muslim says the question could concern the direction of the “fools”: what turned Muslims away from it, namely facing the Kaʿba.
JISHUMI:v1p645/r10.anchor: وقد ذكر أبو مسلم في هذه الآيات الواردة في نسخ القبلة تشككا في صلاة النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

STUDYQURAN:2:intro/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:intro/r20.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:intro/r20.claim: It also addresses the qiblah, the direction one faces during canonical prayer.
STUDYQURAN:2:intro/r20.anchor: one should face while reciting the canonical prayers.

BURSEVI:v1p197/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p197/r1.speaker: التتارخانية
BURSEVI:v1p197/r1.claim: If prayer begins sincerely and ostentation enters later, it follows the original intention; one who prays or beautifies prayer only before people earns the basic prayer’s reward, not its excellence.

BURSEVI:v1p197/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p197/r2.speaker: بعض الحكماء
BURSEVI:v1p197/r2.claim: A sage compares ostentatious worship to carrying a bag of pebbles to market: it earns praise from people but no real benefit.
BURSEVI:v1p197/r2.anchor: قال بعض الحكماء : مثل من يعمل الطاعة للرياء والسمعة

BURSEVI:v1p197/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p197/r3.speaker: الحديث
BURSEVI:v1p197/r3.claim: A report urges people to purify their deeds for God, who accepts only what is sincerely for Him, and warns against claiming a deed is for God and kin when it is not.
BURSEVI:v1p197/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث "أخلصوا أعمالكمتعالى فإن الله لا يقبل إلا ما خلص له ولا تقولوا

BURSEVI:v1p197/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p197/r4.speaker: أحاديث المشارق
BURSEVI:v1p197/r4.claim: A report curses those who curse their parents and those who sacrifice to other than God.
BURSEVI:v1p197/r4.anchor: أحاديث المشارق "لعن الله من لعن والديه ولعن الله من ذبح لغير الله"

BURSEVI:v1p197/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p197/r5.speaker: النووي
BURSEVI:v1p197/r5.claim: Al-Nawawī explains sacrifice to other than God as slaughter done in the name of another, such as an idol or Moses.
BURSEVI:v1p197/r5.anchor: قال النووي المراد الذبح باسم غير الله كمن ذبح للصنم أو لموسى

BURSEVI:v1p197/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p197/r6.speaker: إبراهيم المراودي
BURSEVI:v1p197/r6.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Marwādhī says Bukhara jurists deemed slaughtering for a ruler’s arrival, as a devotional approach to him, forbidden because it was offered to someone besides God.
BURSEVI:v1p197/r6.anchor: ذكر الشيخ إبراهيم المراودي : إن ما يذبح عند استقبال السلطان تقربا إليه

BURSEVI:v1p197/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p197/r7.speaker: الرافعي
BURSEVI:v1p197/r7.claim: Al-Rāfiʿī rejects that ruling: the slaughter celebrates the ruler’s arrival, like an ʿaqīqa for a newborn, so it is not forbidden.
BURSEVI:v1p197/r7.anchor: وقال الرافعي : هذا غير محرم لأنهم إنما يذبحونه استبشارا بقدومه

BURSEVI:v1p197/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p197/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p197/r8.claim: The author adopts al-Rāfiʿī’s charitable reading of Muslims’ actions to protect them from charges of unbelief or wasted deeds; a monotheist seeks God’s approval through available acts of worship.
BURSEVI:v1p197/r8.anchor: وعليه تحمل أفعال المسلمين صيانة لهم عن الكفر وضياع الأعمال

BURSEVI:v1p197/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p197/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p197/r9.claim: The “foolish” are people of weak understanding, especially unbelievers among hypocrites, Jews, and polytheists who object to the qibla change; they are foolish for turning from Abraham’s religion.

BURSEVI:v1p197/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p197/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p197/r10.claim: The advance warning prepares believers, reducing the shock of the expected objection and supplying an answer before the need arises; preparation is better before an opponent’s attack.
BURSEVI:v1p197/r10.anchor: وفائدة تقديم الإخبار به قبل وقوعه ليوطئوا عليه أنفسهم فلا يضطربوا عند وقوعه

BURSEVI:v1p197/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p197/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p197/r11.claim: The question “what turned them” is an emphatic interrogative; the wording distinguishes turning away from something from turning someone toward another thing.
BURSEVI:v1p197/r11.anchor: ما استفهامية إنكارية مرفوعة المحل على الابتداء ووليهم خبره

BURSEVI:v1p197/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p197/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p197/r12.claim: Qibla first meant a person’s facing direction, then in religious usage the direction faced in prayer; it is named from facing it, and here means Jerusalem, replaced by the Kaʿba.
BURSEVI:v1p197/r12.anchor: والقبلة في الأصل الحالة التي عليها الإنسان من الاستقبال فنقلت في عرف الشرع في الجهة التي يستقبلها الإنسان للصلاة

BURSEVI:v1p198/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p198/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p198/r1.claim: The Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for about seventeen months after arriving in Medina to draw the Jews’ hearts, after which the Kaʿba became the Muslims’ qibla until the end of time.
BURSEVI:v1p198/r1.anchor: روي أن النبي عليه السلام صلى إلى نحو بيت المقدس بعد مقدمه المدينة نحوا من سبعة عشر شهرا

BURSEVI:v1p198/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p198/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p198/r2.claim: The answer is that east and west, indeed all places, belong to God; no direction has an inherent claim to be qibla, and it becomes one only by God’s command.

BURSEVI:v1p198/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p198/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p198/r3.claim: God can command facing any direction at any time through His sovereignty and will, and the creature should obey without seeking extra qualities in the commanded act.
BURSEVI:v1p198/r3.anchor: فله أن يأمر في كل وقت بالتوجه إلى جهة من تلك الجهات على حسب ألوهيته واستيلائه ونفاذ قدرته ومشيئته

BURSEVI:v1p198/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p198/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p198/r4.claim: God’s rulings and acts are not driven by causes or purposes; the command calls for compliance, since He is not answerable for what He does.
BURSEVI:v1p198/r4.anchor: لا تجري العلل والأغراض الداعية له تعالى إلى الأمر لأن أحكام الله تعالى وأفعاله ليست معللة

BURSEVI:v1p198/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p198/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p198/r5.claim: Jews chose the west from their own desire because they thought Moses had been on the western side, while Christians chose the east because Mary withdrew eastward.
BURSEVI:v1p198/r5.anchor: واليهود إنما استقبلوا جهة المغرب واتخذوها قبلة اتباعا لهوى أنفسهم

BURSEVI:v1p198/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p198/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p198/r6.claim: Believers faced the Kaʿba in obedience rather than by their own ranking of directions, although it is Abraham’s qibla and Muhammad’s birthplace.
BURSEVI:v1p198/r6.anchor: والمؤمنون استقبلوا الكعبة طاعةتعالى وامتثالا لأمره

BURSEVI:v1p198/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p198/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p198/r7.claim: The straight path is facing Jerusalem at one time and the Kaʿba at another; its straightness lies in its wisdom and benefit.
BURSEVI:v1p198/r7.anchor: وهو التوجه إلى بيت المقدس تارة والكعبة أخرى ووجه استقامته كونه مشتملا على الحكمة والمصلحة

BURSEVI:v1p198#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p198#2/r1.speaker: بعض أرباب الحقيقة
BURSEVI:v1p198#2/r1.claim: Some spiritual masters call the opponents foolish because their minds are veiled from Islam’s truth; sound reason and recognition of comprehensive divine unity would have ended their objection to the change.
BURSEVI:v1p198#2/r1.anchor: قال بعض أرباب الحقيقة : سمى الطاغين من اليهود والمشركين

ELMALILI:2:142-145/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r1.claim: Qibla originally means a person's facing or turning toward any direction, and by convention names the place faced in prayer; in Turkish it means direction.
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r1.anchor: “Kıble”, esasen insanın herhangi bir tarafa teveccüh ve istikbâli hâlidir ki Türkçe “yön” demektir. Örfen namazda teveccüh olunan mekâna isim olmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:142-145/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r2.claim: God announces the change of qibla, guidance to a new straight path, and formation of a new community, while declaring ignorant criticism of the change ineffective.
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r2.anchor: kıblenin tehavvülüne ve yeni bir sırât-ı müstakīmin irâesine ve bu suretle yeni bir ümmet teşkîline işaret

ELMALILI:2:142-145/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r3.speaker: Yehûd veya münafıkīn
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r3.claim: The question about who turned them from their former qibla was voiced by Jews or hypocrites seeking to deny abrogation and object to the change; the verse was revealed concerning them.
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r3.anchor: Bu söz neshi inkâr ve tahvîl-i kıbleye itiraz etmek isteyen Yehûd veya münafıkīn tarafından sarf edilmiş ve âyet onlar hakkında nâzil olmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:142-145/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r4.claim: Although the critics may be Jews or hypocrites, the author finds the hypocrite reading more fitting in light of the earlier declaration that hypocrites are truly the fools.
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r4.anchor: Bâlâda أَلَآ إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ [el-Bakara 2/13][^1] hükm-i celîline nazaran münafıkīn hakkında olması daha münâsibdir.

ELMALILI:2:142-145/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r5.claim: Allah guides whom He wills to the new straight path, since He owns the directions and is not confined by place.
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r5.anchor: dilediği kimseyi yeni bir sırât-ı müstakīme hidâyet eder, muvaffak kılar.

ELMALILI:2:142-145/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r6.claim: The guidance to a straight path directly answers and closely connects with al-Fātiḥa's prayer for guidance to the straight path.
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r6.anchor: Burada doğrudan doğru Fâtiha’daki ٱهْدِنَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ duasına sarih bir alâka, dakīk bir cevap vardır.

ELMALILI:2:142-145/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r7.claim: The indefinite phrase “a straight path” signals a great and new path, better than the one requested and the path of those previously favored, leading more safely and easily to bliss, free from anger and misguidance.
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r7.anchor: Sırât-ı müstakīmin nekre olarak îrâdı, bunun azametine ve yeniliğine bir işarettir

ELMALILI:2:142-145/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r8.claim: Guidance to this path is tied explicitly to divine will because granting it initially is pure grace, independent of human acquisition; in ordinary acquisition, divine will follows human will, while with gifted foundations human acquisition follows divine will.
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r8.anchor: bu sırât-ı müstakīme hidâyet, sırf meşiyyet-i ilâhiyeye rabt edilmiştir. Hilkatte meşiyyet-i ilâhiyeye merbut olmayan hiçbir şey bulunmadığı hâlde bunun tasrîhi

ELMALILI:2:142-145/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r9.claim: God may choose someone as prophet and grant a wholly new religion and law by sheer will; prophethood is not acquired, and the rule of 2:286 applies only after this gift.
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r9.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah her şeye mâliktir ve dilediği kulunu mahz-ı meşiyyetiyle peygamber yapar ve ona büsbütün yeni bir din ve şeriat ihsan edebilir

ELMALILI:2:142-145/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r10.claim: Since God gave Muhammad this guidance, there is no ground to object to His command to change the qibla.
ELMALILI:2:142-145/r10.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak Resûlü Muhammed’e bu hidâyeti bahşetmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r1.claim: Sefih, plural sufaha, is the opposite of halim and can mean ignorant, foolish, crude, or aggressive; Turkish renderings include dim-witted, narrow-minded, and barbarous.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r1.anchor: halîmin zıddı olup “hem cahil ve ahmak hem de kaba ve saldırgan” anlamına gelir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r2.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r2.claim: Exegetes variously identify the “fools” as Jews, pagan Arabs, hypocrites, or all three groups.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r2.anchor: tefsirlerde “cahiller, ahmaklar, kıt akıllılar” şeklinde açıklanmış ve bununla da yahudilerin, putperest Araplar’ın veya münafıkların ya da her üç zümrenin kastedildiği hususunda farklı görüşler ileri sürülmüştür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r3.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r3.claim: Razi recounts that after the Hijra Muhammad prayed toward Jerusalem for a time, pleasing the Jews; the change to the Kaaba then displeased them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r3.anchor: Râzî’nin açıklamalarına göre Hz. Peygamber, Medine’ye hicret ettikten sonra bir süre Kudüs’teki Beytülmakdis’e yönelerek namaz kılmıştı; yahudiler de bundan memnundu.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r4.claim: The commentary recounts that pagan Arabs disliked the Jerusalem direction, then welcomed the Kaaba as qibla but misread it as Muhammad seeking agreement with them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r4.anchor: Müşrik Araplar ise Resûlullah’ın Kudüs’e yönelmesinden hoşnutsuzluk duyuyorlardı. Bu yüzden Kâbe’nin kıble yapıldığı haberinin Mekke’ye ulaşması üzerine bundan memnun oldular

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r5.speaker: Münafıklar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r5.claim: Hypocrites argued that directions did not differ and the qibla change had no reasonable basis, treating Muhammad’s decision as arbitrary mockery.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r5.anchor: Münafıklar da yönlerin birbirinden farkı bulunmadığını, dolayısıyla kıble değiştirmenin mâkul bir gerekçesi olamayacağını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r6.claim: The people behind such views are called fools because their claims sprang from ignorance and envy.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r6.anchor: cahillik ve kıskançlıktan kaynaklanan bu tür görüş ve iddiaların sahipleri “sefihler” diye nitelenmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r7.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r7.claim: Some exegetes infer from the use of sufaha for hypocrites in 2:13 that hypocrites are probably meant here too.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r7.anchor: bu sûrenin 13. âyetinde “süfehâ’” kelimesinin özellikle münafıklar için kullanıldığını dikkate alarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r8.claim: Although hypocrites are a plausible identification, the historical context makes Jews the likelier target.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r8.anchor: Ancak tarihî bağlama göre yahudilerin kastedilmesi ihtimali daha büyüktür.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r9.claim: The answer that east and west belong to God means no place is inherently a qibla: God, its true owner, appoints the direction, and he chose Mecca’s Sacred Mosque instead of Jerusalem’s Bayt al-Maqdis.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r9.anchor: “Doğu da batı da Allah’ındır” buyurularak, hiçbir mekânın kendiliğinden kıble olamayacağına, bunu oranın gerçek sahibi ve mâliki olan Allah’ın tayin edeceğine

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r10.claim: As guiding whomever he wills to the straight path, appointing a qibla is within God’s absolute power and will and should not trouble reasonable people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r10.anchor: İnsanlardan dilediğini dosdoğru yola, kendi yoluna iletmek gibi, dilediği yönü kıble tayin etmek de mutlak güç ve irade sahibi olan Allah’ın yetkisindedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r11.claim: Sirat al-mustaqim means a straight, just, measured, moderate, balanced way of belief and life, free of deviation, excess, and misguidance.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r11.anchor: her türlü eğrilik, aşırılık ve sapıklıktan uzak, dosdoğru, adaletli, ölçülü, ılımlı ve dengeli bir yol, bir inanç ve yaşama biçimi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r12.claim: Linking the qibla change with the straight path links it to Islam and marks the qibla as an Islamic emblem with a subtle meaning fools cannot grasp.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r12.anchor: kıble değişikliğinin “dosdoğru yol” ile ve dolayısıyla İslâm’la irtibatlandırılması, kıblenin İslâmî bir şiâr olduğuna

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r13.claim: Qibla means direction lexically and, as an Islamic term, the specific place faced during prayer—the Kaaba; facing it is called istiqbal al-qibla and is a condition for valid prayer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r13.anchor: Sözlükte “yön” anlamına gelen kıble İslâmî bir terim olarak “namaz sırasında kendisine doğru dönülen özel mekân”ı, yani Kâbe’yi ifade eder.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r14.speaker: İslâm bilginleri
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r14.claim: Scholars require a person who can see the Kaaba to face it precisely, while most jurists say those far away need only face its general direction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r14.anchor: İslâm bilginlerine göre, Kâbe’yi görebilen birinin tam olarak Kâbe’ye dönmesi gerekir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r15.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r15.claim: The Prophet’s report that the area between east and west is qibla means deviations up to 45 degrees on either side do not invalidate prayer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r15.anchor: Nitekim Hz. Peygamber, “Doğu ile batı arası kıbledir” buyurmuşlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r16.claim: If one cannot ask anyone or find a qibla marker, one should estimate from celestial positions or wind; discovering the error after prayer does not invalidate it, while noticing mid-prayer requires turning without interrupting.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r16.anchor: bilgi alacağı bir kimse veya kıbleyi gösteren bir işaret bulamazsa güneş, ay veya yıldızların konumuna yahut rüzgârın yönüne bakarak kıbleyi belirlemeye çalışır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r17.claim: When no direction can be determined, or illness, disability, or fear makes facing qibla impossible or dangerous, one may pray toward any convenient direction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r17.anchor: Araştırmasına rağmen kıblenin yönü konusunda hiçbir kanaate varamayan; aynı şekilde hastalık, sakatlık, düşman korkusu gibi zaruretler dolayısıyla kıbleye dönmesi imkânsız veya tehlikeli olan kimse ise kolayına gelen bir tarafa yönelerek namazını kılar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r18.claim: Travelers on mounts or vehicles who cannot get down at every prayer and cannot combine prayers should face qibla as far as possible when beginning obligatory or necessary prayers aboard.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:142/r18.anchor: namaza başlarken imkân ölçüsünde kıbleye dönerek araç üzerinde farz ve vâcip namazlarını kılarlar.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p41#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p41#2/r3.speaker: البراء
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p41#2/r3.claim: The Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months while wishing to face the Kaaba; after the qibla changed, Jews asked what had turned Muslims from their former direction.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p41#2/r3.anchor: عن البراء قال: لما قدم رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فصلى نحو بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا أو سبعة عشر شهرا

QIRAAT-ER:2:142:22#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:142:22#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:142:22#1/r1.claim: The sīn for ṣād reading is a canonical letter substitution with no semantic difference, only a shift from emphatic to plain sibilant.
QIRAAT-ER:2:142:22#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant with sīn instead of ṣād — ibdāl (letter substitution); no semantic change, phonetic variation between emphatic ṣ and plain s

QIRAAT-ER:2:142:22#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:142:22#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:142:22#2/r1.claim: Ishmām blends ṣād toward zāy, producing an intermediate articulation without a difference in meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:2:142:22#2/r1.anchor: Canonical variant with ishmām (blending ṣ toward z sound) — intermediate articulation between ṣād and zāy; phonetic but no semantic difference

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r2.speaker: البراء بن عازب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r2.claim: The Prophet faced Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months after arriving in Medina, wished to face the Kaaba, and then received the revelation directing him toward it; Jews asked what had turned them from their former qibla.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r2.anchor: رواه البخاري، عن البراء بن عازب قال: لما قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة، فصلى نحو بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r3.claim: The passage answers Jews and Christians who claimed Abraham and the earlier believers belonged to their religions; because Jews denied abrogation, they called the qibla change false and foolish, and God distinguishes guidance from folly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r3.anchor: لأن النسخ عند اليهود باطل، فقالوا: الانتقال عن قبلتنا باطل وسفه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r4.claim: On the apparent future reading, God foretold the Jews' objection before the order to face the Kaaba, making it a prediction of the unseen and preparing the Prophet and Muslims for the objection with an answer ready.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r4.anchor: وذلك قبل أن يؤمروا باستقبال الكعبة، وتكون هذه الآية متقدمة في النزول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r5.claim: An alternative chronology places the order to face the Kaaba before this verse in revelation, although this verse comes first in the recitation; Ibn Abbas and others state this, and the Barāʾ report supports it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r5.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أنها متقدمة في التلاوة، متأخرة في النزول، وأنه نزل قوله: قد نرى تقلب وجهك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r6.claim: The Barāʾ report supports the later-revelation chronology; on it, the future means they persist in an objection already made, while reading سيقول as قال is too strained because of the future marker سـ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r6.anchor: ويدل على هذا ويصححه حديث البراء المتقدم، الذي خرجه البخاري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r7.speaker: البراء بن عازب، مجاهد، ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r7.claim: They identify the foolish objectors as the Jews.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r7.anchor: والسفهاء: اليهود، قاله البراء بن عازب، ومجاهد، وابن جبير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r8.speaker: أبو صالح، عن ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r8.claim: He identifies the objectors as Meccans, who claimed Muhammad missed his birthplace and would soon return to their religion; al-Zajjāj preferred this view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r8.anchor: وأهل مكة قالوا: اشتاق محمد إلى مولده، وعن قريب يرجع إلى دينكم، رواه أبو صالح، عن ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r9.speaker: السدي، عن ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r9.claim: He identifies the objectors as hypocrites mocking the Muslims; the verse's wording also recalls the description of hypocrites in 2:13, or may cover the three groups mentioned earlier.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r9.anchor: أو المنافقون قالوا: ذلك استهزاء بالمسلمين، ذكره السدي، عن ابن مسعود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r10.claim: The qualifier من الناس specifies humans because سفه can describe lightly woven cloth, a light fast spear, and animals; without it, attributing speech to nonhumans could be metaphorical.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r10.anchor: وخص بقوله من الناس، لأن السفه أصله الخفة، يوصف به الجماد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r1.claim: The pronoun in ما ولاهم refers to the Prophet and believers turned from their qibla; it is attributed to them because they had faced it for a long time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r1.anchor: والضمير عائد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، والمؤمنين عن قبلتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r2.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r2.claim: Most exegetes say the change criticized was from Jerusalem to the Kaaba, but the author denies that this is unanimous.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r2.anchor: وأجمع المفسرون على أن هذه التولية كانت من بيت المقدس إلى الكعبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r3.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r3.claim: Some hold that the earlier qibla was the Kaaba, faced when prayer was first prescribed because it was Abraham's qibla; after the Prophet turned toward Jerusalem, Meccans reproached him for leaving it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r3.anchor: بل قد ذهب قوم إلى أن هذه القبلة، التي عيب التحول منها إلى غيرها هي الكعبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r4.claim: The phrase التي كانوا عليها implies sustained commitment to facing the qibla; على is figurative, as though the qibla were something continuously borne or maintained.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r4.anchor: والاستعلاء هنا مجاز، وحكمته الهم لمواظبتهم على امتثال أمر الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r5.claim: The pronouns may instead refer to the foolish objectors: Jews faced west, Christians east, and Arabs had no prayer direction, so they objected when Muhammad faced the Kaaba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r5.anchor: وقيل: يحتمل أن يكون الضمير عائدا على السفهاء، فإنهم كانوا لا يعرفون إلا قبلة اليهود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r6.claim: One view, attributed to Ibn Abbas, says the Jerusalem qibla was established by recited revelation; the author also lists an unrecited divine command and divine permission to choose, with al-Rabīʿ saying the Prophet chose Jerusalem.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r6.anchor: الأول: عن ابن عباس، روي عنه أنه قال: أول ما نسخ من القرآن القبلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r7.speaker: الحسن، عكرمة، أبو العالية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r7.claim: They hold that the Prophet chose Jerusalem by personal reasoning without revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r7.anchor: أو باجتهاده بغير وحي، قاله الحسن وعكرمة وأبو العالية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r8.claim: Reports give the Jerusalem-facing period as sixteen or seventeen months, nine or ten months, or thirteen months; another reckoning begins with the prescribed daily prayers after the Night Journey and ends in Rajab, Jumada, or mid-Shaʿban of year two.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10/r8.anchor: وكذلك اختلفوا في المدة التي صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيها إلى بيت المقدس، فقيل: ستة عشر شهرا، أو سبعة عشر شهرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed two noon rakʿas, then turned toward the Kaaba for the last two.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r1.anchor: وروي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى ركعتي الظهر، فانصرف بالآخرتين إلى الكعبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r2.claim: The verse is evidence that the Qurʾan can abrogate Sunnah, since the Jerusalem-facing prayer was not prescribed in Qurʾanic text, and that abrogation is not a change of mind in God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r2.anchor: وقد استدل بهذه الآية على جواز نسخ السنة بالقرآن، إذ صلاته إلى بيت المقدس ليس فيها قرآن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r3.claim: The command teaches the Prophet how to refute the objection: all directions belong to God, who may require worshippers to face whichever one He chooses as a qibla.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r3.anchor: أن الجهات كلها لله تعالى، يكلف عباده بما شاء أن يستقبل منها، وأن تجعل قبلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r4.claim: East refers to Jerusalem and west to the Kaaba, since the Kaaba lies west of Jerusalem.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r4.anchor: والمغرب بالكعبة، لأن الكعبة غربي بيت المقدس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r5.claim: يهدي من يشاء means those whom God wills to guide; هدى can take لام, إلى, or no preposition, and here it takes إلى.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r5.anchor: يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم: أي من يشاء هدايته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r6.claim: Exegetes disagree whether the qibla was changed during the dawn, noon, or afternoon prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r6.anchor: وقد اختلفوا في الصلاة التي حولت القبلة فيها، فقيل: الصبح، وقيل: الظهر، وقيل: العصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r7.claim: He declines speculative explanations of the qibla change's wisdom when neither revelation nor sound reasoning supports them, warning that seeking causes for divine acts invites error.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r7.anchor: بأشياء لا يقوم على صحتها دليل، وعللوا ذلك بعلل لم يشر إليها الشرع، ولا قاد نحوها العقل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r8.claim: Only wisdoms stated or indicated by revelation, or reached by sound reasoning, should be accepted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r8.anchor: وأما ما نص الشرع على حكمته، أو أشار، أو قاد إليه النظر الصحيح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r9.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r9.claim: Some interpret the straight path here as the Kaaba qibla; the author says the apparent meaning is Islam and its laws, of which the Kaaba is one.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p10#2/r9.anchor: وقد فسر قوله: صراط مستقيم بأنه القبلة التي هي الكعبة. والظاهر أنه ملة الإسلام وشرائعه

QASHANI:2:142/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:142/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:142/r1.claim: The objectors are fools because their minds cannot grasp Islam’s truth and judge only by the beliefs they already know.
QASHANI:2:142/r1.anchor: سماهم سفهاء خفاف العقول، لعدم وفاء عقولهم بإدراك حقيقة دين الإسلام

QASHANI:2:142/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:142/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:142/r2.claim: Their dispute with Muslims despite shared belief in God ignores Muslims’ distinctive sincerity; recognizing the truth would end the dispute.
QASHANI:2:142/r2.anchor: محاجتهم في الله مع اتفاقهم في التوحيد واختصاص المسلمين بالإخلاص

QASHANI:2:142/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:142/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:142/r3.claim: Sound minds would use the signs to discern the truth in each religion and distinguish it from adherents’ falsehood; Islam is wholly true and the truth of truths.
QASHANI:2:142/r3.anchor: لو كانت عقولهم رزينة لاستدلت بالآيات وأدركت في كل دين ومذهب حقه

QASHANI:2:142/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:142/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:142/r4.claim: The community is made a just, excellent witness over other nations.
QASHANI:2:142/r4.anchor: جعلوا أمة وسطا أي: عدلا بين الأمم، فضلاء شهداء عليهم

QASHANI:2:142/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:142/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:142/r5.claim: The objectors were bound to a direction and accepted only a restricted orientation, rather than the unity that encompasses every direction.
QASHANI:2:142/r5.anchor: لأنهم كانوا مقيدين بالجهة فلم يقبلوا إلا مقيدا ولم يعرفوا التوحيد الوافي بالجهات كلها

QASHANI:2:142/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:142/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:142/r6.claim: The straight path is the path of unity: directions are equal in relation to the Real, who is in no direction while all directions are in, through, and for Him.
QASHANI:2:142/r6.anchor: طريق الوحدة التي تتساوى الجهات بالنسبة إليها لكون الحق المتوجه إليه لا في جهة

QASHANI:2:142/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:142/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:142/r7.claim: The verse “wherever you turn, there is God’s face” supports this account of directionless divine unity.

QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r3.claim: Disbelievers’ insight is impaired: they see no correctness in believers’ affairs, disapprove of them, and respond to each new event with a new objection.
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r3.anchor: سقمت بصائر الكفار فلم يلح لهم وجه الصواب في جميع أحوال المؤمنين

QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r4.claim: When the qibla changed to the Kaaba, objectors asked why the believers had turned away if their previous direction was true.
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r4.anchor: فمن ذلك تغير أمر القبلة حينما حولت إلى الكعبة قالوا إن كانت قبلتهم حقا فما الذي ولاهم عنها

QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r5.claim: God owns east and west and directs worshippers toward whichever direction He wills.
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r5.anchor: يتعبد العباد إلى قطر و ( . . . ) ونحو شاؤوا

QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r6.claim: People veiled from witnessing God’s direction of His saints seek rational explanations for their states; seeing all from one perspective would end divided thought and doubt.
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r6.anchor: عن شهود تصريف الحق لأوليائه - يطلبون وجوها من الأمر

QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r7.claim: God guides whomever He wills to His light.
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r7.anchor: ولكن الله يهدي لنوره من شاء

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r1.claim: The fools are either light-minded or people who have degraded their reason through blind imitation and refusal to reflect; the referent broadly includes hypocrites, Jews, and polytheists who reject the qibla change.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r1.anchor: أي الخفاف الأحلام أو المستمهنوها بالتقليد المحض والإعراض عن التدبر والمتبادر منهم ما يشمل سائر المنكرين

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r2.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi restricts the fools to the first group, the hypocrites.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r2.anchor: وروى عن السدي الإقتصار على الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas restricts the fools to the Jews.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r3.anchor: وعن إبن عباس الإقتصار على الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r4.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r4.claim: Al-Hasan restricts the fools to the polytheists.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r5.claim: These reports likely identify groups among those addressed by the revelation rather than restrict its meaning, since the definite plural is general and no reason requires limiting it.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r5.anchor: ولعل المراد بيان طائفة نزلت هذه الآية في حقهم لا حمل الآية عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r6.claim: Announcing the future accusation in advance prepares the listener, softens the shock, prevents confusion, and readies a more decisive answer; its fulfillment after the prediction is a prophetic sign.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r6.anchor: وتقديم الأخبار بالقول على الوقوع لتوطين النفس به فإن مفاجأة المكروه أشد إيلاما

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r7.claim: A proposed reason for the advance notice is to teach that the statement stems from foolishness and should not cause distress; the author replies that the exchange itself would teach this even after the event.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r7.anchor: الوجه في التقديم هو التعليم والتنبيه على أن هذا القول أثر السفاهة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r8.speaker: القفال
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r8.claim: Al-Qaffal says the verse came after the qibla change and that the future tense means past: enemies had criticized the action and would repeat their criticism.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r8.anchor: وقال القفال : إن الآية نزلت بعد تحويل القبلة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r9.speaker: البراء بن عازب
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r9.claim: Al-Baraʾ reports that the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months after arriving in Medina, wished to face the Kaʿba, and then received the revelation beginning قد نرى تقلب وجهك.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r9.anchor: عن البراء رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : لما قدم رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r10.speaker: البراء بن عازب
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r10.claim: A transmission through Abu Ishaq, ʿUbayd ibn Humayd, and Abu Hatim adds that سيقول السفهاء was revealed as well.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r10.anchor: وفي رواية أبي إسحاق وعبيد بن حميد وأبي حاتم عنه زيادة فأنزل الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r11.claim: The passage follows the previous one as criticism of a subsidiary matter after the earlier criticism of fundamentals; the lack of conjunction shows each is independently scandalous.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2/r11.anchor: ومناسبة الآية لما قبلها أن الأولى قدح في الأصول وهذا في أمر متعلق بالفروع وإنما لم يعطف تنبيها على إستقلال كل منهما

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r1.claim: من الناس is an accusative circumstantial phrase meaning humankind generally; it emphasizes how foolish the accusers are by comparison with the human species.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r1.anchor: في موضع نصب على الحال والمراد منهم الجنس وفائدة ذكره التنبيه على كمال سفاهتهم بالقياس إلى الجنس

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r2.claim: Another reading takes الناس to mean unbelievers and clarifies that the accusation came only from the most depraved among the groups, not every individual.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : الكفرة وفائدته بيان أن ذلك القول المحكي

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r3.claim: The author prefers the generic meaning of people over the restriction to unbelievers.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r4.claim: ما ولاهم means “what turned them away”; its root denotes a second thing following the first without interruption, and the question is reproachful.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r4.anchor: أي أي شيء صرفهم وأصله من الولي وهو حصول الثاني بعد الأول من غير فصل والإستفهام للإنكار

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r5.claim: Their former qibla was Jerusalem; قبلة is derived from facing, originally describing the state of the one faced and conventionally naming the place toward which prayer is directed.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r5.anchor: يعني بيت المقدس وهي فعلة من المقابلة كالوجهة من الواجهة وأصلها الحالة التي كان عليها المقابل

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r6.claim: Describing the qibla as one they had followed, after already calling it theirs, intensifies the rebuke; Jews objected because they denied abrogation and disliked Muhammad's divergence from them.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r6.anchor: وفي وصفها بذلك بعد إضافتها إلى ضمير المسلمين تأكيد للإنكار ومدار هذا الإنكار بالنسبة إلى اليهود زعمهم إستحالة النسخ

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r7.claim: The Jews said that Muhammad should return to their qibla so they would follow and believe; the author suspects this was only an attempt to tempt him.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r7.anchor: أرجع إلى قبلتنا نتبعك ونؤمن بك

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r8.claim: The polytheists sought to attack Islam by claiming that neither facing Jerusalem nor turning away from it had a reason; they said Muhammad abandoned his ancestors' qibla, returned to it, and would return to their religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r8.anchor: وبالنسبة إلى مشركي العرب القصد إلى الطعن في الدين وإظهار أن كلا من التوجه إليها والإنصراف عنها بغير داع إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r9.claim: The hypocrites' objections varied with their backgrounds, since some were Jews and others were not.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r9.anchor: وبالنسبة إلى المنافقين مختلف بإختلاف أصولهم فإن فيهم اليهود وغيرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r10.speaker: البخاري
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r10.claim: A report gives the time facing Jerusalem as sixteen or seventeen months; other reports give nine or ten months from Malik ibn Anas, thirteen from Muʿadh, and seven from al-Sadiq.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r10.anchor: وأختلف الناس في مدة بقائه صلى الله عليه وسلم مستقبلا بيت المقدس ففي رواية البخاري ما علمت

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r11.claim: There are two views on whether the Prophet faced a different qibla in Mecca; the more famous view says he did not, and this is also narrated from al-Sadiq.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r11.anchor: وهل أستقبل غيره قبل بمكة أم لا قولان أشهرهما الثاني وهو المروي أيضا عن الصادق

ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r12.claim: All places and directions belong equally to God; no direction is inherently special to Him, and the relevant matter is obedience, since He may command any place or direction for prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p2#2/r12.anchor: أي جميع الأمكنة والجهات مملوكة له تعالى مستوية بالنسبة إليه عز شأنه لا إختصاص لشيء منها به

ALUSI-FULL:v2p3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p3/r1.claim: The straight path is a level road and means what divine wisdom requires: facing Jerusalem at one time and the Kaʿba at another.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p3/r1.anchor: أي طريق مستو وهو ما تقتضيه الحكمة من التوجه إلى بيت المقدس تارة وإلى الكعبة أخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v2p3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p3/r2.claim: The guidance clause is an appositional substitute of inclusion from the preceding statement; it explains what justifies the turn toward the Kaʿba, while the earlier clause justifies the former direction.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p3/r2.anchor: والجملة بدل إشتمال مما تقدم وهو إشارة إلى مصحح التولية وهذا إلى مرجحها

ALUSI-FULL:v2p3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p3/r3.claim: God chose the community for this guidance, so they praise Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p3/r3.anchor: يخص الله تعالى بها من يشاء ويختار من عباده وقد خصنا بها فله الحمد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r3.claim: “Turned them” means redirected or changed their direction; their former qibla was Jerusalem.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى: {سيقول السفهاء} الجهال {من الناس ما ولاهم} صرفهم وحولهم {عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها} يعني بيت المقدس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r4.claim: The passage was revealed when Jews and Meccan polytheists criticized the shift from Jerusalem to Mecca, claiming Muhammad was wavering, longing for his birthplace, and returning to the polytheists' religion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r4.anchor: نزلت في اليهود ومشركي مكة طعنوا في تحويل القبلة من بيت المقدس إلى مكة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r5.claim: The east and west belong to God, and all creatures are His servants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r5.anchor: {قل لله المشرق والمغرب} له والخلق عبيده.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r6.claim: God guides whomever He wills to a straight path.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p158/r6.anchor: يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r1.claim: The ‘fools’ are people of weak understanding who squander it through imitation and refusal to reason, especially hypocrites, Jews, and polytheists opposing the qibla change.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r1.anchor: الذين خفت أحلامهم، واستمهنوها بالتقليد والإعراض عن النظر. يريد به المنكرين لتغيير القبلة من المنافقين واليهود والمشركين.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r2.claim: Foretelling their objection prepares the Prophet for it, readies the answer, and displays a miracle.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r2.anchor: وفائدة تقديم الإخبار به توطين النفس وإعداد الجواب وإظهار المعجزة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r3.claim: Mā wallāhum asks what turned them away.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r5.claim: Qibla originally means one's state of facing and by convention the place toward which one turns in prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r5.anchor: والقبلة في الأصل الحالة التي عليها الإنسان من الاستقبال، فصارت عرفا للمكان المتوجه نحوه للصلاة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r6.claim: East and west belong to God; no place has an inherent feature that prevents another place from taking its place, so obedience to His command matters.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r6.anchor: لا يختص به مكان دون مكان بخاصية ذاتية تمنع إقامة غيره مقامه، وإنما العبرة بارتسام أمره لا بخصوص المكان

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r7.claim: The straight path is the direction endorsed by wisdom and welfare, whether Jerusalem or the Kaaba at a given time.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:142/r7.anchor: وهو ما ترتضيه الحكمة، وتقتضيه المصلحة من التوجه إلى بيت المقدس تارة، والكعبة أخرى.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r1.claim: The opponents invoked their ancestors' religion to preserve their claim that Paradise belonged exclusively to them and to resist abrogation; God's rebuke exposes this as foolishness.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r1.anchor: لما كان ادعاؤهم أن أسلافهم على دينهم لئلا تنتقض دعواهم أن الجنة خاصة بهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r2.claim: Because they know the new direction is true, the objection is brazen; even if they did not know, they should at least refrain from mockery.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r3.claim: Calling them al-sufahāʾ describes people who act without evidence, either by ignoring proof for desire or mistaking something else for proof.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r3.anchor: والسفيه الذي يعمل بغير دليل , إما بأن لا يلتفت إلى دليل فلا يتوقف إلى أن يلوح له بل يتبع هواه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r4.claim: The phrase min al-nās broadens blame beyond Jews or Israelites to everyone who sides with them; al-nās is associated with motion.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r4.anchor: دون أن يقول : من أهل الكتاب , أو بني إسرائيل - ونحو ذلك تصريحا بذمهم وتعميما لكل من مالأهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r5.claim: Saying mā wallāhum rather than asking min intensifies the insult through contempt for those who ask what turned them away.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r5.anchor: { ما ولاهم } ولم يقولوا : من , زيادة في الأذى بالاحتقار

BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r6.claim: Al-Harali defines qibla as what is placed opposite the face, and qibal as the body's front opposite its rear.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r6.anchor: قال الحرالي : القبلة ما تجعل قبالة الوجه , والقبل ما أقبل من الجسد في مقابلة الدبر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r7.claim: The verse leaves the former qibla unnamed so it can also evoke the Kaaba: either the critics fault God's command or they are followers of desire in every case.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r7.anchor: ولعله ترك الإفصاح ليصلح ذلك لإرادة الكعبة أيضا ليصير المعنى : إن كانوا انتقلوا عن الكعبة بأمر الله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r8.claim: The critics had exhausted their arguments and voiced this insinuation to those they had misled among the hypocrites, unable to confront steadfast believers.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p259/r8.anchor: ألقوا هذه الشبهة إلى من اختدعوه من المنافقين ولم يقدروا أن يواجهوا بها أحدا من الثابتي الإيمان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r1.claim: The answer begins with an unaddressed qul, unlike earlier direct challenges in 2:80 and 2:111, because the opponents could not face believers with their insinuation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r1.anchor: ولذا جاء جوابهم بقوله : { قل } خاليا عن خطاب لا كما مضى في قوله :

BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r2.claim: The prediction that enemies would object is a major sign of prophethood: it came true, yet their intense hostility could not make them call it false.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r2.anchor: وساق سبحانه الإخبار عنهم بذلك على طريق هو من أعلام النبوة وجلائل الرسالة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r3.claim: Five earlier arguments prepared for this dispute: scriptural distortion, abrogation, obstruction of the mosque, God's ownership of every direction, and the Kaaba's construction and sanctity; Muslims received the answer in advance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r3.anchor: مع ما في ذلك من توطين نفوس أهل الإسلام وإكرامهم بتعليم الجواب قبل الحاجة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r4.claim: Calling the objectors fools recalls the hypocrites in 2:13: those corrupt outwardly and inwardly are even more foolish than hypocrites who conceal inner corruption.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260/r4.anchor: وتسميتهم سفهاء ناظر غلى قوله فيما مضى عمن نافق منهم ومن غيرهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r1.claim: The Jews' opposition to Abraham's religion, despite claiming agreement with him, recalls the condemnation of one who makes himself a fool in 2:130.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r1.anchor: لما تقرر من مخالفتهم له وإن ادعوا الموافقة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r2.claim: God owns east and west, named as the two horizons that encompass all directions; no direction is inherently exclusive, so whatever orientation He commands is right.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r2.anchor: { المشرق والمغرب } مخصصا لهما لكونهما مجمعي الآفاق كما مضى فلا تختص بالوجهة إليه جهة دون أخرى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r3.claim: The straight path reaches God from any commanded direction; its indefiniteness refers to particular laws, unlike the definite path in al-Fātiḥa, which denotes the whole revealed law.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r3.anchor: فمتى سلكه وصل إلى المقصود من غير ضلال , ونكره لأن المراد به جزئيات من الشريعة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r4.claim: The Kaaba is the earth's middle, built by Abraham, himself the most balanced prophet; it is the best of houses, so the qibla is central in every sense.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p260#2/r4.anchor: لأنها إلى البيت العتيق الذي هو وسط الأرض وهو بناء إبراهيم عليه السلام هو أوسط الأنبياء وهو مع ذلك خيار البيوت

IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r1.speaker: البراء
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r1.claim: Al-Bara says the “fools” are the Jews; Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Hasan are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r1.anchor: عن البراء : سيقول السفهاء قال : اليهود . وروى عن ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن ونحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse about the fools was revealed concerning the hypocrites.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r2.anchor: عن السدى ، فانزل الله في المنافقين : سيقول السفهاء من الناس ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r3.speaker: مجاهد، عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r3.claim: Mujahid and Ata gloss “what turned them” as “what diverted them.”
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد ، تو عن رجل ، عن ابن جريج عن عطاء ، ومجاهد ، يزيد بعضهم على بعض : ما ولاهم ما صرفهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r4.speaker: عطاء بن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r4.claim: The former qibla was Jerusalem, which God abrogated and replaced with the Ancient House.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r4.anchor: عن عطاء بن عباس : سيقول السفهاء من الناس ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها يعنون بيت المقدس ، فنسخها وصرفه الله إلى البيت العتيق .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r5.claim: Jews asked Muhammad to return to Jerusalem, promising to follow and affirm him, but sought to tempt him away from his religion.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r5.anchor: ان يهودا قالوا للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم : يا محمد ، ما ولاك عن قبلتك التي كنت عليها وانت تزعم انك على ملة إبراهيم ودينه ، ارجع إلى قبلتك التي كنت عليها نتبعك ونصدقك ، وانما يريدون فتنته عن دينه

IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r6.speaker: البراء بن عازب
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r6.claim: The Prophet had faced Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months, wished to face the Kaaba, and changed direction after revelation; the Jews then questioned the change.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r6.anchor: كان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم قد صلى نحو بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا أو سبعة عشر شهرا ، وكان يجب ان يوجه نحو الكعبة ، فانزل الله تعالى : قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام

IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r7.speaker: البراء بن عازب
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r7.claim: After the change, the Jews questioned the new qibla, and God replied that east and west belong to Him and He guides whom He wills.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p247/r7.anchor: وقال السفهاء من الناس - وهم اليهود - ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانواعليها ؟ فانزل الله : قل لله المشرق والمغرب يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p248/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p248/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p248/r1.claim: After the migration, God directed the Prophet to face Jerusalem, pleasing the Jews; he longed for Abraham's qibla, prayed while looking heavenward, and was turned toward the Kaaba.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p248/r1.anchor: ان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم لما هاجر إلى المدينة امره الله ان يستقبل بيت المقدس ، ففرحت اليهود فاستقبلها رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم بضعة عشر شهرا ، وكان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم يحب قبلة إبراهيم ، فكان يدعو لله وينظر إلى السماء

IBNABIHATIM:v1p248/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p248/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p248/r2.claim: The change made the Jews doubt and question the Prophet, after which the verse states that God owns east and west and guides whom He wills.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p248/r2.anchor: فارتاب من ذلك اليهود وقالوا : قل لله المشرق والمغرب يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p248/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p248/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p248/r3.claim: God guides whom He wills to a way out of doubts, misguidance, and temptation.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p248/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية ، في قول الله : يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم يقول : يهديهم إلى المخرج من الشبهات والضلالات والفتنة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r1.claim: Some commentators assign the west to the Jews and the east to Christians as their respective prayer directions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r1.anchor: الذين نسبوا إلى اليهود استقبال جهة المغرب وإلى النصارى استقبال جهة المشرق من المفسرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r2.claim: On that reading, naming east and west either avoids a fruitless contest over directions, since all belong to God, or alludes to Islam's superior qibla.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r2.anchor: فيكون الجواب جوابا بالإعراض عن ترجيح قبلة المسلمين لعدم جدواه هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r3.claim: The straight path means a means to good and whatever leads to it, including guidance to the better direction; it echoes the prayer in 1:6.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r3.anchor: والمراد بالصراط المستقيم هنا وسيلة الخير وما يوصل إليه كما تقدم في قوله تعالى : { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم } ( الفاتحة : 6 ) فيشمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r4.claim: The clause about guiding whom He wills is circumstantial from God's name; reading it as an explicative substitute is unclear because ownership of all directions does not entail guidance being God's alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r4.anchor: فجملة : { يهدي من يشاء } حال من اسم الجلالة ولا يحسن جعلها بدل اشتمال من جملة : { لله المشرق والمغرب }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r5.claim: Muslim scholars agree that facing the Kaaba is required for valid obligatory and voluntary prayer, with necessity exceptions for obligatory prayer and a travel concession for voluntary prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r5.anchor: واتفق علماء الإسلام على أن استقبال الكعبة أي التوجه إليها شرط من شروط صحة الصلاة المفروضة والنافلة إلا لضرورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r6.claim: Inside the Sacred Mosque one must face the Kaaba itself; in Mecca, those who can see it face its visible side, and long rows must curve around it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r6.anchor: فأما الذي هو في المسجد الحرام ففرض عليه استقبال عين الكعبة من أحد جوانبها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r7.speaker: ابن القصار
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r7.claim: For worshippers who cannot see the Kaaba, Ibn al-Qassar requires aiming at its exact axis, a difficult standard that may require astronomical instruments; Malikis also transmit this from al-Shafi'i.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r7.anchor: وهذا قول ابن القصار واختاره أحد أشياخ أبي الطيب عبد المنعم الكندي ونقله المالكية عن الشافعي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r8.speaker: أكثر المالكية والأبهري والباجي وأبو حنيفة وأحمد بن حنبل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r8.claim: The majority view is to face the Kaaba's general direction, as if a straight walk would reach its vicinity; Ibn Ashur favors this easier view as removing hardship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r8.anchor: وهذا قول أكثر المالكية واختاره الأبهري والباجي وهو قول أبي حنيفة وأحمد بن حنبل وهو من التيسير ورفع الحرج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r9.speaker: ابن القاسم عن مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r9.claim: People in Medina may use the Prophet's prayer place as their direction; Malik reportedly said Gabriel established the qibla of the Prophet's mosque.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p13/r9.anchor: وروى ابن القاسم عن مالك أن جبريل هو الذي أقام للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم قبلة مسجده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.claim: God announces that people will ask why believers turned from their former Syrian direction toward the Kaaba; safīh describes lightness in judgment and intellect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.anchor: أعلم الله تعالى في هذه الآية أنهم سيقولون في شأن تحول المؤمنين من الشام إلى الكعبة: ما ولاهم؟ والسفهاء هم الخفاف الأحكام والعقول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.claim: Safah conveys lightness or looseness, as in a poorly woven garment; Dhu al-Rumma's verse uses تسفهت for being made light by wind.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.anchor: والسفه الخفة والهلهلة، ثوب سفيه أي غير متقن النسج، ومنه قول ذي الرمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.claim: The phrase من الناس specifies the group because foolishness also describes inanimate things and animals; the fools are all who asked what turned them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.anchor: وخص بقوله من الناس، لأن السفه يكون في جمادات وحيوانات، والمراد ب السفهاء هنا جميع من قال ما ولاهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jewish scholars asked Muhammad why he had left their qibla and offered to believe if he returned, intending to tempt him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: «قالها الأحبار منهم» ، وذلك أنهم جاؤوا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا: يا محمد ما ولاك عن قبلتنا؟

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says some Jews and hypocrites mocked the change, saying Muhammad longed for his homeland.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.anchor: وقال السدي: قالها بعض اليهود والمنافقون استهزاء، وذلك أنهم قالوا: اشتاق الرجل إلى وطنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.claim: Another group identifies the speakers as Quraysh disbelievers, who claimed he returned because he knew they were right and would rejoin their religion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.anchor: وقالت طائفة: قالها كفار قريش، لأنهم قالوا: ما ولاه عن قبلته؟ ما رجع إلينا إلا لعلمه أنا على الحق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.claim: ولاهم means turned them away; qibla names the posture or manner of facing something, like sitting or girding.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.anchor: وولاهم معناه صرفهم، والقبلة فعلة هيئة المقابل للشيء، فهي كالقعدة والإزرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.claim: The future form سيقول replaces the past to convey that the critics persist in saying this; Ibn Abbas and others state the verse came after their statement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.anchor: وجعل المستقبل موضع الماضي في قوله سيقول دلالة على استدامة ذلك، وأنهم يستمرون على ذلك القول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas and others state that the verse was revealed after the critics had already spoken.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r9.anchor: ونص ابن عباس وغيره أن الآية نزلت بعد قولهم.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r10.claim: God's ownership of East and West is an argument that all places belong to Him; His guidance here directs this community to Abraham's qibla, and ṣirāṭ means road.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p217#2/r10.anchor: أي له ملك المشارق والمغارب وما بينهما، ويهدي من يشاء، إشارة إلى هداية الله تعالى هذه الأمة إلى قبلة إبراهيم، والصراط: الطريق.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r1.speaker: ابن فورك عن ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r1.claim: Ibn Furak transmits from Ibn Abbas that the qibla was the first thing abrogated in the Quran.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r1.anchor: فذكر ابن فورك عن ابن عباس قال: أول ما نسخ من القرآن القبلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r2.claim: The majority say the Jerusalem qibla was commanded through non-recited revelation, rather than Quranic text.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r2.anchor: وقال الجمهور: بل كان أمر قبلة بيت المقدس بوحي غير متلو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r3.speaker: الربيع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r3.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the Prophet was given a choice of directions and chose Jerusalem to cultivate relations with the People of the Book.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r3.anchor: وقال الربيع: خير رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في النواحي فاختار بيت المقدس، ليستألف بها أهل الكتاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r4.speaker: من قال كان بوحي غير متلو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r4.claim: Those who say the qibla came through non-recited revelation explain it as a test of Arabs, who were used to the Kaaba and disliked Jerusalem.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r4.anchor: ومن قال كان بوحي غير متلو قال: كان ذلك ليختبر الله تعالى من آمن من العرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r5.speaker: البخاري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r5.claim: A report in al-Bukhari gives the duration facing Jerusalem as sixteen or seventeen months.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r5.anchor: ففي البخاري: ستة عشر أو سبعة عشر شهرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r6.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r6.claim: A report from Anas ibn Malik gives nine or ten months facing Jerusalem.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r6.anchor: وروي عن أنس بن مالك: تسعة أو عشرة أشهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r7.speaker: غيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r7.anchor: وروي عن غيره: ثلاثة عشر شهرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r8.speaker: مكي عن إبراهيم بن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r8.claim: Makki transmits a chronology from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq: prayer began in Mecca as two units morning and evening; after the Isra, on 17 Rabiʿ al-Thani a year before the Hijra, five daily prayers were prescribed, Gabriel led the first noon prayer toward Jerusalem, and the Prophet continued facing it in Medina until Rajab, or according to other reports Jumada or mid-Shaʿban, year two.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p218/r8.anchor: وحكى مكي عن إبراهيم بن إسحاق أنه قال: أول أمر الصلاة أنها فرضت بمكة ركعتين في أول النهار وركعتين في آخره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r1.speaker: البراء بن عازب، مجاهد، سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r1.claim: One identification of the foolish people is the Jews.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r1.anchor: انهم اليهود قاله البراء بن عازب و مجاهد وسعيد ابن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r2.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r2.claim: A second identification is the people of Mecca.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r2.anchor: انهم أهل مكة رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r3.speaker: السدي عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r3.claim: A third identification is the hypocrites.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r3.anchor: انهم المنافقون ذكره السدي عن اين مسعود وابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r4.claim: All three groups may have made the objection; the verse came after the qibla was changed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r4.anchor: وقد يمكن أن يكون الكل قالوا ذلك والاية نزلت بعد تحويل القبلة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r5.claim: Sufahāʾ means ignorant people, and the question asks who turned them away from the former Jerusalem qibla.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r5.anchor: والسفهاء الجهلة ما ولاهم أي صرفهم عن قبلتهم يريد قبلة المقدس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r6.speaker: البراء بن عازب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r6.claim: One report gives the period of prayer toward Jerusalem after arrival in Medina as sixteen or seventeen months.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r6.anchor: أنه ستة عشر شهرا أو سبعة عشر قاله البراء به عازب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas gives the period toward Jerusalem as seventeen months.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r7.anchor: سبعة عشر شهرا قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r8.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r8.claim: Muʿādh ibn Jabal gives the period toward Jerusalem as thirteen months.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r8.anchor: ثلاثة عشر شهرا قاله معاذ بن جبل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r9.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r9.claim: Anas ibn Malik gives the period toward Jerusalem as nine or ten months.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r9.anchor: تسعة اشهر أو عشرة أشهر قاله أنس بن مالك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r10.claim: One of two reports from Qatada gives the period as sixteen months.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r10.anchor: والخامس ستة عشر شهرا والسادس ثمانية عشر شهرا روي القولان عن قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r11.claim: The other report from Qatada gives the period as eighteen months.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r11.anchor: والخامس ستة عشر شهرا والسادس ثمانية عشر شهرا روي القولان عن قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r12.claim: One view says the first qibla toward Jerusalem was set by God’s command and revelation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r12.anchor: أنه كان بأمر الله تعالى ووحيه قاله ابن عباس وابن جريج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r13.speaker: الحسن، أبو العالية، عكرمة، الربيع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r13.claim: Another view says the Prophet chose Jerusalem by his own reasoning and judgment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r13.anchor: أنه كان باجتهاده ورأيه قاله الحسن و أبوالعالية وعكرمة والربيع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r14.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r14.claim: Qatada says people initially faced any direction under the rule that east and west belong to God, then were ordered toward Jerusalem.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r14.anchor: كان الناس يتوجهون إلى أي جهة شاؤوا بقوله ﴿ ولله المشرق والمغرب ﴾ البقرة 115 ثم أمرهم باستقبال بيت المقدس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r15.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r15.claim: One explanation for choosing Jerusalem was to win over the People of the Book.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r15.anchor: ليتألف أهل الكتاب ذكره بعض المفسرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r16.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r16.claim: A second explanation is that the unfamiliar direction would test the Arabs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p153#2/r16.anchor: لامتحان العرب بغير ما ألفوه قاله الزجاج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r1.speaker: البراء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r1.claim: Al-Bara reports that the Prophet faced Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months, then people turned toward the Kaaba during prayer after a worshipper announced the change; Bukhari gives this route and Muslim another.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r1.anchor: عن البراء، رضي الله عنه؛ أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى إلى بيت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports that the Prophet watched the sky awaiting revelation, received the command to face the Kaaba, and Muslims asked about deceased believers' earlier prayers; the response was 2:143, followed by the question about the change in 2:142.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r3.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: حدثني إسماعيل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r4.speaker: البراء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r4.claim: In Ibn Ishaq's account, the foolish questioners are the People of the Book, who ask what turned the Muslims from their former qibla.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r4.anchor: وقال السفهاء من الناس، وهم أهل الكتاب: ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r5.speaker: البراء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r5.claim: Al-Bara's report through Israel identifies the questioners as Jews and says the answer was that God owns east and west and guides whom He wills.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p452/r5.anchor: وقال السفهاء من الناس، وهم اليهود: {ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها} فأنزل الله {قل لله المشرق والمغرب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet was commanded to face Jerusalem after migrating, though he loved Abraham's qibla, prayed and looked to heaven, then received the command to face the Kaaba; Jews objected to the change.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما هاجر إلى المدينة، أمره الله أن يستقبل بيت المقدس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir synthesizes the reports: at Mecca the Prophet could face Jerusalem's rock while standing between the Kaaba's corners; after migration he faced Jerusalem because both directions could not be combined.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r2.anchor: فكان بمكة يصلي بين الركنين، فتكون بين يديه الكعبة وهو مستقبل صخرة بيت المقدس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r3.claim: The authorities differ whether the command to face Jerusalem came through Qur'anic revelation or another means.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r3.anchor: ثم اختلف هؤلاء هل كان الأمر به بالقرآن أو بغيره؛ على قولين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r4.claim: Ikrima, Abu al-Aliyah, and al-Hasan al-Basri hold that the Prophet's orientation toward Jerusalem arose from his own judgment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة وأبي العالية والحسن البصري أن التوجه إلى بيت المقدس كان باجتهاده عليه الصلاة والسلام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r5.claim: After sixteen-plus months, God answered the Prophet's repeated supplication to face the Kaaba, and he announced the change to the people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r5.anchor: وكان يكثر الدعاء والابتهال أن يوجه إلى الكعبة، التي هي قبلة إبراهيم، عليه السلام، فأجيب إلى ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r6.speaker: البراء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r6.claim: Bukhari's report from al-Bara says the first prayer toward the Kaaba was Asr, while al-Nasaʾi's report from Abu Saʿid ibn al-Muʿalla says it was Dhuhr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r6.anchor: وكان أول صلاة صلاها إليها صلاة العصر، كما تقدم في الصحيحين من رواية البراء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r7.claim: Ibn Umar reports that Quba learned of the command on the following morning during Fajr and turned from Syria toward the Kaaba while praying.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p453/r7.anchor: عن ابن عمر أنه قال: بينما الناس بقباء في صلاة الصبح، إذ جاءهم آت فقال: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قد أنزل عليه الليلة قرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r1.claim: A repealed rule binds only after people learn of its repeal, even if the new revelation has already come and been conveyed; the earlier prayers were not ordered repeated.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r1.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على أن الناسخ لا يلزم حكمه إلا بعد العلم به، وإن تقدم نزوله وإبلاغه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r2.claim: Hypocrites, doubters, and Jews became unsettled and asked why the Muslims sometimes faced one direction and sometimes another.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r2.anchor: وقالوا: {ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها} أي: ما لهؤلاء تارة يستقبلون كذا، وتارة يستقبلون كذا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r3.claim: God answers that direction and command belong to Him; obedience consists in following His orders wherever He directs, even if direction changes repeatedly. Ibn Kathir links this to 2:177.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r3.anchor: أي: الحكم والتصرف والأمر كله لله، وحيثما تولوا فثم وجه الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r4.speaker: author
