IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r4.claim: God honored Muhammad and his community by guiding them to Abraham's qibla, the Kaaba, the most honored house on earth, built by Abraham for God alone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r4.anchor: وجعل توجههم إلى الكعبة المبنية على اسمه تعالى وحده لا شريك له، أشرف بيوت الله في الأرض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r5.claim: The Prophet says the People of the Book envy Muslims for Friday, the qibla God guided them to, and saying amin behind the imam; Aisha transmits the report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p454/r5.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم -يعني في أهل الكتاب -:"إنهم لا يحسدوننا على شيء كما يحسدوننا على يوم الجمعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457/r1.claim: God first directed Muhammad toward Jerusalem, then toward the Kaaba, to reveal who follows the Messenger and who turns back from the faith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457/r1.anchor: إنما شرعنا لك -يا محمد -التوجه أولا إلى بيت المقدس، ثم صرفناك عنها إلى الكعبة، ليظهر حال من يتبعك ويطيعك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457/r6.claim: At Quba, a man announced that revelation had ordered the Kaaba as qibla, and the congregation turned toward it during the dawn prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457/r6.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: بينا الناس يصلون الصبح في مسجد قباء إذ جاء رجل فقال: قد أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457#2/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457#2/r1.claim: A version says the worshippers were bowing when they turned together toward the Kaaba while remaining in bowing posture.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457#2/r1.anchor: وعنده: أنهم كانوا ركوعا، فاستداروا كما هم إلى الكعبة، وهم ركوع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457#2/r2.claim: Their immediate turn demonstrates complete obedience to God and compliance with His command.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p457#2/r2.anchor: وهذا يدل على كمال طاعتهم لله ورسوله، وانقيادهم لأوامر الله عز وجل

NAHHAS:v1p268/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p268/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p268/r1.claim: السفهاء is the plural of سفيه; the feminine plural is سفايه.

NAHHAS:v1p268/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p268/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p268/r2.claim: ما in ما ولاهم is a full noun functioning as subject, and ولاهم is its predicate.
NAHHAS:v1p268/r2.anchor: ما اسم تام في موضع رفع بالابتداء وولاهم في موضع الخبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r1.speaker: اليهود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r1.claim: The fools may be Jews who disliked facing the Kaaba and denied the possibility of abrogation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r1.anchor: وهم اليهود لكراهتهم التوجه إلى الكعبة وانهم لا يرون النسخ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r2.speaker: المنافقون
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r2.claim: Another identification is the hypocrites, eager to find grounds for criticism and mockery.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r2.anchor: وقيل المنافقون لحرصهم على الطعن والاستهزاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r3.speaker: المشركون
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r3.claim: A third identification is the polytheists, who said Muhammad first rejected his fathers' qibla, then returned, and would return to their religion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r3.anchor: وقيل المشركون قالوا رغب عن قبلة آبائه ثم رجع اليها والله ليرجعن إلى دينهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r4.claim: Announcing their objection in advance softens the shock, prepares believers for it and supplies a ready answer that more effectively silences the opponent.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r4.anchor: فائدته ان مفاجأة المكروه أشد والعلم به قبل وقوعه أبعد من الاضطراب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r5.claim: The question asks who turned them away; the former qibla was Jerusalem.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r5.anchor:
﴿ ما ولاهم ﴾
ما صرفهم
﴿ عن قبلتهم ﴾
وهي بيت المقدس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r6.claim: The east and west mean the lands in those directions and the whole earth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r6.anchor: أي بلاد المشرق والمغرب والأرض كلها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p223#4/r7.claim: God guides whom He wills from among the earth's inhabitants.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p224/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p224/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p224/r1.claim: The straight path is the wise and beneficial choice to direct the community first to Jerusalem and then to the Kaaba.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p224/r1.anchor: وهو ما توجبه الحكمة والمصلحة من توجيههم تارة إلى بيت المقدس وأخرى إلى الكعبة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r1.claim: Safīh, plural sufahāʾ, means light of judgment, compared with lightly woven cloth and a spear that penetrates quickly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r1.anchor: السفهاء : واحده سفيه , والسفيه : الخفيف الحلم , من قولهم ثوب سفيه إذا كان خفيف النسج , ورمح سفيه إذا أسرع نفوذه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r2.claim: The “fools” may be the Jews, according to Mujahid.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r3.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r3.claim: The “fools” may be the hypocrites, according to al-Suddi.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj reports the view that the “fools” are Quraysh unbelievers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r5.claim: The question asks what turned Muslims away from their former qibla, Jerusalem, which the Prophet faced in Mecca and after the migration to Medina.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r5.anchor: يعني ما صرفهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها , وهي بيت المقدس , حيث كان يستقبلها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r6.speaker: البراء بن عازب
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r6.claim: Al-Bara ibn ʿAzib reports the Prophet faced Jerusalem for sixteen months after the migration.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r6.anchor: بعد هجرته إلى المدينة بستة عشر شهرا في رواية البراء بن عازب

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r7.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r7.claim: A report from Muʿadh ibn Jabal gives thirteen months facing Jerusalem.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r7.anchor: وفي رواية معاذ بن جبل : ثلاثة عشر شهرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r8.claim: A report from Anas ibn Malik gives nine or ten months facing Jerusalem.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r8.anchor: وفي رواية أنس بن مالك تسعة أشهر أو عشرة أشهر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r9.speaker: أنس بن مالك
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r9.claim: According to Anas, the change to the Kaaba came in a noon prayer in Medina after two rakʿas toward Jerusalem; the Prophet turned his face to the Kaaba.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r9.anchor: ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمدينة في صلاة الظهر وقد صلى منها ركعتين نحو بيت المقدس , فانصرف بوجهه إلى الكعبة , هذا قول أنس بن مالك

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r10.speaker: البراء بن عازب
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r10.claim: Al-Bara says that during the second rakʿa of the afternoon prayer at Quba, a passerby testified the Prophet had prayed toward Mecca, so worshippers turned toward the House while bowing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r10.anchor: وقال البراء بن عازب : كنا في صلاة العصر بقباء , فمر رجل على أهل المسجد وهم ركوع في الثانية

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r11.claim: Scholars disagree whether the Prophet faced Jerusalem by God's command, as Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jurayj say, or by personal judgment, as al-Hasan, ʿIkrima, Abu al-ʿAliya, and al-Rabi say.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r11.anchor: واختلف أهل العلم في استقبال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيت المقدس , هل كان برأيه واجتهاده , أو كان عن أمر الله تعالى

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r12.speaker: أبو جعفر الطبري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r12.claim: Al-Tabari says Jerusalem was chosen to win over the People of the Book.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r12.anchor: أحدهما : أنه اختار بيت المقدس ليتألف أهل الكتاب , وهذا قول أبي جعفر الطبري

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r13.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r13.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the unfamiliar Jerusalem qibla tested Arabs accustomed to the Kaaba, revealing who followed and who turned back.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r13.anchor: والثاني : لأن العرب كانت تحج البيت غير آلفة لبيت المقدس , فأحب الله أن يمتحنهم بغير ما ألفوه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Rifaʿa ibn Qays, Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, al-Rabi, and Kinana ibn Abi al-Huqayq challenged the change and offered to follow Muhammad if he returned to the former qibla, intending to tempt him away from his religion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r14.anchor: قال ابن عباس : أتى رفاعة بن قيس وكعب بن الأشرف والربيع وكنانة بن أبي الحقيق , فقالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ما ولاك عن قبلتك

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r15.claim: God owns east and west and commands people to face whichever direction He orders; the straight path is an even road.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p196#2/r15.anchor: يعني حيثما أمر الله تعالى باستقباله من مشرق أو مغرب والصراط : الطريق : والمستقيم : المستوي

MUJAHID:v1p90/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p90/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p90/r1.claim: The foolish people who questioned the change of qibla were the Jews, referring to the move away from Jerusalem.
MUJAHID:v1p90/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال ﴿ السفهاء من الناس ﴾ هم اليهود

MUJAHID:v1p90/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p90/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p90/r2.claim: The question about what turned them means: what diverted them from their former qibla.
MUJAHID:v1p90/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي جريح عن مجاهد ﴿ ما ولاهم ﴾ يقول ما صرفهم

MUQATIL:2:142-143/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r1.claim: Before the five prayers, Muhammad and his companions prayed two units at dawn and dusk in Mecca; after the Night Ascent five prayers were prescribed, with two units for travelers and four for residents.
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r1.anchor: كانوا بمكة يصلون ركعتين بالغداة وركعتين بالعشى، فلما عرج بالنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى السماء ليلا

MUQATIL:2:142-143/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r2.claim: After migrating to Medina, the Prophet was ordered to pray toward Jerusalem so the People of the Book would not deny him, since they found his description in the Torah; Muslims prayed that way for seventeen months, while the Ansar had done so for two years before the Hijra.
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r2.anchor: فصلى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه قبل بيت المقدس من أول مقدمه المدينة سبعة عشر شهرا

MUQATIL:2:142-143/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r3.claim: The Kaaba was the Prophet's preferred qibla; he told Gabriel he wished God would turn him away from the Jews' qibla, and Gabriel said he was only a servant and advised him to ask God.
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r3.anchor: وددت أن ربى صرفنى عن قبلة اليهود إلى غيرها

MUQATIL:2:142-143/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r4.claim: Gabriel ascended while the Prophet kept looking toward heaven in hope of an answer; in Rajab, during the first prayer and two months before Badr, God ordered him to face the Kaaba.
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r4.anchor: فأنزل الله عز وجل فى رجب عند صلاة الأولى قبل قتال بدر بشهرين

MUQATIL:2:142-143/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r5.claim: Meccan polytheists claimed the Prophet had changed direction from longing for his ancestral birthplace and would return to their religion; Muqatil calls this foolishness.
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r5.anchor: قال مشركو مكة: قد تردد على أمره واشتاق إلى مولد آبائه،

MUQATIL:2:142-143/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r6.claim: The fools are Meccan polytheists who asked what turned the Muslims from their former qibla; east and west belong to God, who guides whom He wills to Islam.
MUQATIL:2:142-143/r6.anchor: يعنى مشركي مكة، { ما ولاهم } ، يقول: ما صرفهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r1.claim: The fools are identified as Jews angry at facing the Kaaba and unwilling to accept abrogation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r1.anchor: هم اليهود لكراهتمهم التوجه إلى الكعبة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r2.claim: Alternatively they are hypocrites, eager to attack and ridicule.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r2.anchor: أو المنافقون لحرصهم على الطعن والاستهزاء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r3.claim: Alternatively they are polytheists who mocked Muhammad for leaving his ancestral qibla and returning, predicting he would return to their religion.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r3.anchor: المشركون لقولهم رغب عن قبلة آبائه ثم رجع اليها والله ليرجعن إلى دينهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r4.claim: Announcing their objection before it occurs prepares the audience, since advance warning makes an unpleasant event less jarring and a prepared answer more effectively silences an opponent.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r4.anchor: وفائدة الإخبار بقولهم قبل وقوعه توطين النفس إذ المفاجأة بالمكروه أشد وعداد الجواب قبل الحاجة إليه أقطع للخصم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r5.claim: The former qibla was Jerusalem; qibla means the direction a person faces in prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r5.anchor: يعنون بيت المقدس والقبلة الجهة التى يستقبلها الإنسان فى الصلاة لأن المصلى يقابلها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r6.claim: The east and west mean their lands, and the whole earth belongs to God.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r6.anchor: بلاد الشرق والمغرب و الأرض كلها له

NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r7.claim: The straight path may mean guidance to the true qibla, the Kaaba.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r7.anchor: يرشد من يشاء إلى قبلة الحق وهى الكعبة التى أمرنا بالتوجه إليها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r8.claim: Alternatively, all places belong to God, who may command facing Jerusalem at one time and the Kaaba at another, without objection.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p75/r8.anchor: الأماكن كلها لله فيأمر بالتوجه إلى حيث شاء فتارة الكعبة وطورا إلى البيت المقدس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r1.claim: God foretells objections to turning believers from Syria toward the Kaaba; the future 'will say' is used like past speech to show the objection persists.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r1.anchor: أعلم الله تعالى أنهم سيقولون في تحويل المؤمنين من الشام إلى الكعبة: ما ولاهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r2.claim: 'Among people' is specified because foolishness may also be attributed to inanimate things and animals; the fools are all who ask why Muslims were redirected.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r2.anchor: وخص بقوله: «من الناس» لأن السفه يكون في جمادات وحيوانات.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r3.speaker: المؤرج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r3.claim: Al-Muʾarrij defines safīh as a slanderous liar who deliberately contradicts what he knows.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r3.anchor: وقال المؤرج: السفيه البهات الكذاب المتعمد خلاف ما يعلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r4.speaker: قطرب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r4.claim: Quṭrub defines safīh as extremely unjust and ignorant.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r5.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r5.claim: Mujāhid identifies the fools as the Jews of Medina.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r5.anchor: والمراد بالسفهاء هنا اليهود الذين بالمدينة قاله مجاهد.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r6.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r6.claim: Al-Suddī identifies them as the hypocrites.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r7.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj identifies them as Quraysh, who said Muhammad longed for his birthplace and would soon return to their religion; Jews alleged he was confused, while hypocrites mocked the change.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r7.anchor: الزجاج: كفار قريش لما أنكروا تحويل القبلة قالوا: قد اشتاق محمد إلى مولده

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r8.claim: Wallāhum means that God turned or redirected them from their former direction.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r9.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that people praying dawn at Qubāʾ were told the Prophet had been ordered to face the Kaaba, so they turned from Syria toward it; Mālik transmits this wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r9.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: بينما الناس بقباء في صلاة الصبح إذ جاءهم آت فقال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r10.speaker: البراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r10.claim: Al-Barāʾ reports in al-Bukhārī that the Prophet faced Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months, wished to face the House, and a worshipper told another mosque during prayer; they turned toward the Kaaba while bowing.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r10.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى إلى بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا أو سبعة عشر شهرا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r11.speaker: البراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r11.claim: Al-Barāʾ adds that people who died before the qiblah changed left uncertainty about their status, and the report then introduces a Qur'anic revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142/r11.anchor: وكان الذي مات على القبلة قبل أن تحول قبل البيت رجال قتلوا لم ندر ما نقول فيهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r2.claim: Another account says the Prophet faced Jerusalem to win the Jews over, then wished to turn to the Kaaba when their hostility became clear; Ibn ʿAbbas says the Kaaba was Abraham’s qibla.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r2.anchor: لما قدم المدينة أراد أن يستألف اليهود فتوجه إلى قبلتهم ليكون ذلك أدعى لهم فلما تبين عنادهم وأيس منهم أحب أن يحول إلى الكعبة فكان ينظر إلى السماء وكانت محبته إلى الكعبة لأنها قبلة إبراهيم عن ابن عباس.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r3.claim: A reported reason for preferring the Kaaba is that it would draw the Arabs toward Islam.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: لأنها كانت أدعى للعرب إلى الإسلام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says the change was intended to oppose the Jews.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r5.speaker: أبو العالية الرياحي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r5.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya al-Riyahi says Salih’s mosque faced the Kaaba and Moses prayed toward the rock in the direction of the Kaaba, which was the prophets’ qibla.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r5.anchor: وروي عن أبي العالية الرياحي أنه قال: كانت مسجد صالح عليه السلام وقبلته إلى الكعبة قال: وكان موسى عليه السلام يصلي إلى الصخرة نحو الكعبة، وهي قبلة الأنبياء كلهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r6.claim: The verse clearly proves that God’s rulings and the Qurʾan include abrogation and replacement; the community agrees except for a dissenting outlier.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r6.anchor: في هذه الآية دليل واضح على أن في أحكام الله تعالى وكتابه ناسخا ومنسوخا، وأجمعت عليه الأمة إلا من شذ

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r7.claim: Scholars agree that the qibla was the first Qurʾanic ruling abrogated; one of the earlier accounts says it was abrogated twice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r7.anchor: وأجمع العلماء على أن القبلة أول مانسخ من القرآن، وأنها نسخت مرتين، على أحد القولين المذكورين في المسألة قبل.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r8.claim: The episode proves that the Qurʾan may abrogate a Sunna: the Prophet faced Jerusalem by Sunna, then this Qurʾanic command replaced it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r8.anchor: ودلت أيضا على جواز نسخ السنة بالقرآن وذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r9.claim: On that account, كنت عليها is understood as أنت عليها, meaning that the Prophet is now facing the qibla.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r9.anchor: وعلى هذا يكون: { كنت عليهآ } بمعنى أنت عليها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r10.claim: The people of Quba accepted one messenger’s report of the changed qibla and turned from the established direction, showing action on an individual report.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r10.anchor: وفيها دليل على جواز القطع بخبر الواحد وذلك أن استقبال بيت المقدس كان مقطوعا به من الشريعة عندهم، ثم أن أهل قباء لما أتاهم الآتي وأخبرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r11.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r11.claim: Abu Hatim holds that relying on one report is rationally possible if the law commands it and that it occurred during the Prophet’s lifetime, as the Quba episode shows.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r11.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: والمختار جواز ذلك عقلا لو تعبد الشرع به، ووقوعا في زمن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بدليل قصة قباء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r12.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r12.claim: Abu Hatim says individual governors conveyed abrogating and abrogated rulings to people, while after the Prophet’s death an individual report cannot replace Qurʾanic or mass-transmitted knowledge by consensus.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r12.anchor: وبدليل أنه كان عليه السلام ينفذ آحاد الولاة إلى الأطراف وكانوا يبلغون الناسخ والمنسوخ جميعا. ولكن ذلك ممنوع بعد وفاته صلى الله عليه وسلم، بدليل الإجماع من الصحابة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r13.speaker: من منع ذلك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r13.claim: Those who reject abrogation by an individual report argue that it would entail the impossible replacement of something definitive by something conjectural.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r13.anchor: احتج من منع ذلك بأنه يفضي إلى المحال وهو رفع المقطوع بالمظنون.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r14.claim: The Quba and governor reports are explained by accompanying indications that conveyed knowledge, either actually or by reasonable inference.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r14.anchor: وأما قصة أهل قباء وولاة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فمحمول على قرائن إفادة العلم إما نقلا وتحقيقا، وإما احتمالا وتقديرا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r15.claim: The author prefers that a person remains bound by the earlier ruling until the abrogating ruling reaches them, because Quba kept facing Jerusalem until the messenger arrived.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#2/r15.anchor: وفيها دليل على أن من لم يبلغه الناسخ إنه متعبد بالحكم الأول خلافا لمن قال: إن الحكم الأول يرتفع بوجود الناسخ لا بالعلم به، والأول أصح لأن أهل قباء لم يزالوا يصلون إلى بيت المقدس إلى أن أتاهم الآتي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r1.claim: An abrogating ruling takes effect once it exists, but only for someone who knows it, because a legal address does not address one to whom it has not reached.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r1.anchor: فالناسخ إذا حصل في الوجود فهو رافع لا محالة لكن بشرط العلم به لأن الناسخ خطاب، ولا يكون خطابا في حق من لم يبلغه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r2.claim: The dispute affects whether worship performed after abrogation but before notice must be repeated, and also bears on an agent acting before learning of the principal’s death or dismissal, a financial partner, and a judge.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r2.anchor: وفائدة هذا الخلاف في عبادات فعلت بعد النسخ وقبل البلاغ هل تعاد أم لا وعليه تنبني مسألة الوكيل في تصرفه بعد عزل موكله أو موته وقبل علمه بذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r3.claim: The sound view is that an agent’s transactions and a judge’s rulings in that interval stand and are not overturned.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r3.anchor: والصحيح أن ما فعله كل واحد من هؤلاء ينفذ فعله ولا يرد حكمه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r4.speaker: القاضي عياض
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r4.claim: Qadi ʿIyad says a person freed without knowing remains legally treated as free in dealings with others, and the act is valid before God.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r4.anchor: قال القاضي عياض: ولم يختلف المذهب في أحكام من أعتق ولم يعلم بعتقه أنها أحكام حر فيما بينه وبين الناس، وأما بينه وبين الله تعالى فجائزة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r5.claim: The jurists agree that a woman freed during prayer before she learns of her freedom need not repeat prayers performed without covering.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r5.anchor: ولم يختلفوا في المعتقة أنها لا تعيد ما صلت بعد عتقها وقبل علمها بغير ستر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r6.claim: They disagree about a condition that changes worship while it is underway; the author says the worshipper completes the prayer and what has passed counts.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r6.anchor: وإنما اختلفوا فيمن يطرأ عليه موجب يغير حكم عبادته وهو فيها، قياسا على مسألة قباء فمن صلى على حال ثم تغيرت به حاله تلك قبل أن يتم صلاته إنه يتمها ولا يقطعها ويجزيه ما مضى.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r7.claim: Examples of completing the prayer include someone unclothed who finds clothing, a healthy worshipper who becomes ill, an ill person who recovers, someone seated who can stand, and a slave woman freed during prayer who covers herself and continues.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r7.anchor: وكذلك كمن صلى عريانا ثم وجد ثوبا في الصلاة، أو ابتدأ صلاته صحيحا فمرض، أو مريضا فصح، أو قاعدا ثم قدر على القيام، أو أمة عتقت وهي في الصلاة إنها تأخذ قناعها وتبني.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r8.claim: The author adds that Malik, al-Shafiʿi, and others say a person who finds water while praying with tayammum does not interrupt the prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r8.anchor: وكمن دخل في الصلاة بالتيمم فطرأ عليه الماء إنه لا يقطع، كما يقوله مالك والشافعي رحمهما الله وغيرهما.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r9.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that finding water during a tayammum prayer requires interrupting it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r9.anchor: وقيل: يقطع وهو قول أبي حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى، وسيأتي.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r10.claim: The verse also supports accepting an individual report; the early community agreed, as the Prophet routinely sent individual governors and messengers to teach religion and convey commands and prohibitions.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r10.anchor: وفيها دليل على قبول خبر الواحد، وهو مجمع عليه من السلف معلوم بالتواتر من عادة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في توجيهه ولاته ورسله آحادا للآفاق ليعلموا الناس دينهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r11.claim: The Qurʾan descended in successive portions as needs arose until God completed the religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r11.anchor: وفيها دليل على أن القرآن كان ينزل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شيئا بعد شيء وفي حال بعد حال، على حسب الحاجة إليه، حتى أكمل الله دينه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r12.claim: God’s ownership of the east, west, and what lies between them proves that He may command worshippers to face whichever direction He chooses.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r12.anchor: أقامه حجة أي له ملك المشارق والمغارب وما بينهما فله أن يأمر بالتوجه إلى أي جهة شاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r13.claim: The phrase about guidance points to God guiding this community to Abraham’s qibla; the straight path is a road without crookedness.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:142#3/r13.anchor: إشارة إلى هداية الله تعالى هذه الأمة إلى قبلة إبراهيم والله تعالى أعلم.

SAMIN-DURR:2:142/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:142/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:142/r1.claim: من الناس is a circumstantial phrase from السفهاء governed by سيقول; Ibn Atiyya and others say it specifies people because foolishness and figurative speech can also be attributed to nonhuman things.
SAMIN-DURR:2:142/r1.anchor: { من الناس }: في محل نصب على الحال، من " السفهاء " والعامل فيها " سيقول " وهي حال مبينة

SAMIN-DURR:2:142/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:142/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:142/r2.claim: ما is interrogative and the following sentence predicates it; عن قبلتهم attaches to ولاهم, while عليها omits a noun such as their orientation or belief, and metaphorically portrays their observance as being on top of the qibla.
SAMIN-DURR:2:142/r2.anchor: قوله: { ما ولاهم } " ما " مبتدأ وهي استفهامية، والجملة بعدها خبر عنها، و " عن قبلتهم " متعلق ب " ولاهم "

RAZI-FULL:v4p82#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p82#2/r1.speaker: اليهود والنصارى
RAZI-FULL:v4p82#2/r1.claim: Jews and Christians argue that abrogation entails either God's ignorance or His misleading people: an unqualified command lasts once, a temporary one is not abrogated, and revoking an explicitly permanent command implies either a change in knowledge or deception.
RAZI-FULL:v4p82#2/r1.anchor: النسخ يقتضي إما الجهل أو التجهيل

RAZI-FULL:v4p82#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p82#2/r2.speaker: اليهود والنصارى
RAZI-FULL:v4p82#2/r2.claim: They further argue that qibla directions are equally God's creation, so changing between them lacks a change in benefit and is purposeless, which they say is inconsistent with divine wisdom.
RAZI-FULL:v4p82#2/r2.anchor: الجهات متساوية في أنها لله تعالى ومخلوقة له فتغيير القبلة من جانب فعل خال عن المصلحة

RAZI-FULL:v4p82#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p82#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p82#2/r3.claim: Razi identifies the challenge to the qibla change as an argument by which these groups seek to discredit Islam, and turns to explaining the wording before answering it as the Quran does.
RAZI-FULL:v4p82#2/r3.anchor: فتوصلوا بهذا الوجه إلى الطعن في الإسلام

RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r1.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r1.claim: Al-Qaffal says the future form can describe a past utterance when it is repeated; reports say the criticism had already been voiced when the verse came down.
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r1.anchor: وهو اختيار القفال أن هذا اللفظ وإن كان للمستقبل ظاهرا لكنه قد يستعمل في الماضي أيضا

RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r2.claim: Alternatively, the verse predicts the criticism before it occurs, demonstrating knowledge of the unseen, easing its hurt, and placing the answer ready for the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r2.anchor: أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام إذا أخبر عن ذلك قبل وقوعه ،

RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r3.claim: A fool cannot distinguish benefit from harm and abandons sound judgment; error in religion is more harmful than worldly error, so every unbeliever is foolish.
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r3.anchor: من لا يميز بين ما له وعليه ، ويعدل

RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r4.claim: They identify the critics as Jews, who expected the Prophet's agreement on the qibla to lead to full agreement; after the change they said he had returned to his forefathers' way.
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد : هم اليهود ، وذلك لأنهم كانوا يأتسون

RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، البراء بن عازب، الحسن، الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r5.claim: They identify the critics as Arab polytheists: in Mecca the Prophet faced Jerusalem, but after turning to the Kaaba in Medina they claimed he had returned to their way.
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس والبراء بن عازب والحسن والأصم ، إنهم مشركو العرب

RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r6.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r6.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the critics as hypocrites, who mocked the shift as arbitrary because no rational feature distinguished one direction from another; the name fools is especially associated with them.
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r6.anchor: وثالثها : أنهم المنافقون وهو قول السدي ، وهؤلاء إنما ذكروا ذلك استهزاء

RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r7.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r7.claim: The Judge says the verse only establishes that some group made this remark, so a universal reading is unnecessary.
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r7.anchor: قال القاضي : المقصود من الآية بيان وقوع هذا الكلام منهم في الجملة

RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r8.claim: The definite plural can include all unbelievers, as reason and 2:130 indicate; the Judge's point does not restrict that scope, and enemies naturally criticize whenever able, so likely all said it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r8.anchor: بل الأقرب أن يكون الكل قد قال ذلك لأن الأعداء مجبولون على القدح والطعن

RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r1.claim: Walla ʿan means to turn someone away from something, unlike wallā ilā; the same usage appears in 8:16.

RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r2.claim: The question “what turned them?” is phrased to express mockery and astonishment.

RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r3.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r3.claim: The well-known, consensus interpretation is that unbelievers mocked the Prophet and believers when God changed their qibla from Jerusalem to the Kaaba.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r3.anchor: المفسرين : أنه لما حولت القبلة إلى الكعبة من بيت المقدس

RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r4.claim: Anas dates the qibla change to nine or ten months after the migration.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r4.anchor: فعن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه بعد تسعة أشهر أو عشرة أشهر

RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r5.speaker: معاذ
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r5.claim: Muadh dates the qibla change to thirteen months after the migration.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r5.anchor: وعن معاذ بعد ثلاثة عشر شهرا

RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r6.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r6.claim: Qatada dates the qibla change to sixteen months after the migration.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r6.anchor: وعن قتادة بعد ستة عشر شهرا

RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، البراء بن عازب
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Bara ibn ʿAzib date the change to seventeen months after the migration; al-Razi says this is the most established report.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس والبراء بن عازب بعد سبعة عشر شهرا

RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r8.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r8.claim: Another report places the change eighteen months after the Prophet's arrival.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r8.anchor: وعن بعضهم ثمانية عشر شهرا من مقدمه

RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r9.speaker: الواقدي
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r9.claim: Al-Waqidi says the qibla changed on Monday, the middle of Rajab, after seventeen months.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r9.anchor: قال الواقدي : صرفت القبلة يوم الاثنين النصف من رجب

RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r10.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r10.claim: Other reports date the change to two years after the migration.

RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r11.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r11.claim: Abu Muslim proposes that “the qibla they had been on” means the fools' familiar Jewish and Christian directions; since they had not customarily prayed toward a set direction, the Prophet's facing the Kaaba surprised them, and God answers that east and west belong to Him.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r11.anchor: قول أب مسلم وهو أنه لما صح الخبر

RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r12.claim: Al-Razi accepts the reported shift from Jerusalem to the Kaaba; without the clear reports, Abu Muslim's alternative remains plausible.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84/r12.anchor: فإنه لولا الروايات الظاهرة لكان هذا القول محتملا والله أعلم

RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r1.claim: Qibla names the direction a person faces; the word derives from facing or mutual encounter.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r1.anchor: القبلة هي الجهة التي يستقبلها الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r2.speaker: قطرب
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r2.claim: Qutrub notes the idiom “he has no qibla,” meaning a person has no direction or refuge to turn to.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r2.anchor: وقال قطرب : يقولون في كلامهم ليس لفلان قبلة ، أي ليس له جهة

RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r3.speaker: غيره
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r3.claim: Another explanation is reciprocal: when two people face one another, each is the other's qibla.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r3.anchor: وقال غيره : إذ تقابل الرجلان فكل واحد منهما قبلة للآخر

RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r4.speaker: بعض المحدثين
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r4.claim: A poetic line uses qibla for the direction or refuge toward which one turns.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r4.anchor: جعلت مأواك لي قرارا … وقبلة حيثما لجأت

RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r5.claim: The first answer to the objection is that every direction belongs to God; none is inherently a qibla, and a direction becomes one only by God's designation, so changing it is unobjectionable.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r5.anchor: فلا يستحق شيء منها لذاته أن يكون قبلة

RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r6.claim: Al-Razi frames two questions: why God initially designated a qibla and why He later changed it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r6.anchor: قلنا : أما المسألة الأولى ففيها الخلاف الشديد بين أهل السنة والمعتزلة

RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r7.speaker: أهل السنة
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r7.claim: Sunnis hold that God's rulings need not be explained by purposes; if a purpose benefits God, He would be deficient, while if benefit is irrelevant to Him it cannot motivate the act.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r7.anchor: أما أهل السنة فإنهم يقولون : لا يجب تعليل أحكام الله تعالى ألبتة

RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r8.speaker: أهل السنة
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r8.claim: They argue that if God can achieve a goal without an intermediary, using the intermediary is futile; if He cannot, that implies incapacity.

RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r9.speaker: أهل السنة
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r9.claim: They argue that an eternal purpose would entail an eternal act, while a created purpose requires another purpose, leading to circularity or an infinite regress.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r9.anchor: توقف إحداثه على غرض آخر ، ولزم الدور أو التسلسل وهو محال

RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r10.speaker: أهل السنة
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r10.claim: They argue that explaining why the world began at a particular time by a special wisdom only repeats the question of why that wisdom arose then; either case calls for a further determiner or none.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r10.anchor: كان طلب العلة في أنه لم حصلت تلك الحكمة في ذلك الوقت دون سائر الأوقات كطلب العلة

RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r11.speaker: أهل السنة
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r11.claim: They argue that all good and evil, faith and unbelief, obedience and sin occur by God's power and will, which rules out a purpose that returns to the servant in creating unbelief and eternally punishing it.

RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r12.speaker: أهل السنة
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r12.claim: They argue that God's eternal will either acts contingently, requiring another cause and regress, or necessarily, in which case it needs no cause.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r12.anchor: إما أن يكون جائزا أو وجبا

RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r13.claim: Al-Razi concludes that God's acts proceed from divinity, power, and sovereignty; the verse grounds abrogation in His ownership of east and west, not in wisdom as the Muʿtazila say.

RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r14.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r14.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that a wise God cannot act without purposes; all acts and rulings have wisdom, sometimes evident and sometimes hidden, so the qibla change may have concealed benefits and does not discredit Islam.
RAZI-FULL:v4p84#2/r14.anchor: أما المعتزلة فقد قالوا : لما دلت الدلائل على أنه تعالى حكيم

RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r1.claim: Al-Razi cautions that proposed wisdoms for the qibla are not conclusive proofs but possibilities.
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r1.anchor: واعلم أن أمثال هذه المباحث لا تكون قطعية ، بل غايتها أن تكون أمورا احتمالية

RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r2.claim: A fixed direction gives imagination a concrete form to help the intellect grasp abstractions, like an engineer's diagram; facing the qibla resembles facing a king, while recitation praises him and bowing and prostration serve him.
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r2.anchor: فاستقبال القبلة في الصلاة يجري مجرى كونه مستقبلا للملك لا معرضا عنه

RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r3.claim: Prayer seeks presence of heart, supported by stillness and avoiding distraction; keeping one direction helps, especially if that direction is regarded as honorable.
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r3.anchor: وهذا لا يتأتى إلا إذا بقي في جميع صلاته مستقبلا لجهة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r4.claim: A shared direction promotes harmony among believers, a blessing named in 5:7; different directions could make them appear divided in worship.
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r4.anchor: أن الله تعالى يحب الموافقة والألفة بين المؤمنين

RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r5.claim: Calling the Kaaba God's house and believers His servants honors both; the worshipper faces God's house physically and God with the heart.
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r5.anchor: يا مؤمن أنت عبدي ، والكعبة بيتي

RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r6.speaker: بعض المشايخ
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r6.claim: Some shaykhs say Jews faced their qibla because Moses was called from the western side (28:44), Christians faced west because Gabriel came to Mary from the east (19:16), while Muslims face the Kaaba, qibla of Abraham and the Prophet's birthplace and sanctuary.
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r6.anchor: قال بعض المشايخ : إن اليهود استقبلوا القبلة لأن النداء لموسى

RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r7.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r7.claim: Others say Christians face the rising lights, while Muslims face Muhammad, the master of lights, from whose light all lights were created.
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r7.anchor: وكان بعضهم يقول : استقبلت النصارى مطلع الأنوار

RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r8.claim: The Kaaba is the earth's center, so directing prayer there symbolizes the duty of justice in all things.
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r8.anchor: الكعبة سرة الأرض ووسطها ، فأمر الله تعالى جميع خلقه

RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r9.claim: The change honors Muhammad, whom the Prophet wished for in opposition to the Jews: God says “a qibla you are pleased with,” suggesting He seeks Muhammad's pleasure in both worlds, as 93:5 promises.
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r9.anchor: ولم يقل قبلة أرضاها ، والإشارة فيه كأنه تعالى قال : يا محمد

RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r10.claim: Al-Razi links the command not to dismiss the poor in 6:52 with this honor: the Kaaba is the direction of Muhammad's face and the poor the direction of God's mercy, so turning away from either is wrongful.
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r10.anchor: الكعبة قبلة وجهك ، والفقراء قبلة رحمتي

RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r11.claim: He describes a hierarchy of qiblas: the Throne for its bearers, the Kursi for the pious, the Frequented House for scribes, the Kaaba for believers, and God for bewildered believers (2:115).
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r11.anchor: وثامنها : العرش قبلة الحملة ، والكرسي قبلة البررة

RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r12.claim: He says the Throne is made of light, the Kursi of pearl, and the Frequented House of ruby; the Kaaba is made from five named mountains, and pilgrimage or prayer toward it expiates sins as heavy as those mountains.
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r12.anchor: وثبت أن العرش مخلوق من النور ، والكرسي من الدر ، والبيت المعمور من الياقوت

RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r13.claim: After listing these possible explanations for designating a qibla, al-Razi says the first is the soundest account.
RAZI-FULL:v4p86/r13.anchor: فهذا جملة الوجوه المذكورة في هذا الباب ، والتحقيق هو الأول

RAZI-FULL:v4p87/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p87/r7.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v4p87/r7.claim: The Muʿtazila define guidance as direction that leads the servant to what is best; the straight path leads to Paradise for those who follow it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p87/r7.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : إنما هي الدلالة الموصلة

RAZI-FULL:v4p87/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p87/r8.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v4p87/r8.claim: Al-Razi's Ashʿari school rejects guidance as mere invitation or indication, since both are general to all accountable people; it must mean God's creation of knowledge, making guidance and misguidance God's acts.
RAZI-FULL:v4p87/r8.anchor: قال أصحابنا : هذه الهداية إما أن يكون المراد منها الدعوة

STUDYQURAN:2:142/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r1.claim: The verse recalls the qiblah discussion at 2:115c: East and West belong to God.
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r1.anchor: See 2:115c, which discusses the qiblah and how the East and the West belong to God.

STUDYQURAN:2:142/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r2.claim: The future “will say” can describe a recurring trait in the past, not only predict a future objection.
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r2.anchor: The use of the future will say in this verse does not exclude its referring to the past, as a kind of trait, and not only a prediction (R).

STUDYQURAN:2:142/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r3.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r3.claim: The prayer direction is not inherently merited by Jerusalem or Makkah; its authority comes from God's command.
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r3.anchor: The verse is meant partly to remind one that it is not the place itself (Jerusalem or Makkah) that merits being the direction of prayer or qiblah, but the fact that God has commanded it to be so (R).

STUDYQURAN:2:142/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r4.claim: After the Hijrah the Prophet faced Jerusalem for between thirteen and twenty months; most reports give sixteen or seventeen.
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r4.anchor: in the reports the number of months varies between thirteen and twenty, but most mention sixteen or seventeen (IK, Q, Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:2:142/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r5.speaker: some accounts
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r5.claim: Some accounts say the Prophet and followers faced the Kaʿbah in Makkah, then Jerusalem briefly after migration, then the Kaʿbah again; others say they faced Jerusalem even in Makkah.
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r5.anchor: Some accounts state that, initially, the Prophet and his followers, while still in Makkah, prayed in the direction of the Kaʿbah, then faced Jerusalem for a brief period after migrating to Madinah, and then faced the Kaʿbah once more. Others aver, however, that even while in Makkah they prayed toward Jerusalem

STUDYQURAN:2:142/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r6.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r6.claim: Some commentators say hypocrites posed the question about the new qiblah cynically and without sincerity.
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r6.anchor: Some commentators believe that it was the hypocrites who asked this question regarding the change in direction and that, as such, they were not sincere but cynical in their intentions (Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:2:142/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r7.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r7.claim: The qiblah change is the first chronological case of Qurʾānic abrogation and a paradigm in which the Qurʾān abrogates Sunnah; see 2:106c.
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r7.anchor: It is the first instance of abrogation in the chronological order of revelation and is often cited as a paradigmatic case, though it is an instance of the Quran abrogating the Sunnah (Q); on naskh, see 2:106c.

STUDYQURAN:2:142/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r8.claim: The mosque of the Two Qiblahs is associated with a report that an announcement of the change came during prayer and the congregation turned mid-prayer.
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r8.anchor: it was reported that in the midst of a prayer, a caller came to announce the change in direction, at which the congregation turned, mid-prayer, and faced the new qiblah

STUDYQURAN:2:142/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r9.claim: Determining the qiblah outside Makkah has long generated debate and several methods.
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r9.anchor: Determining the qiblah in locales outside of Makkah has been and continues to be a subject of lively debate. Several different methods have been employed throughout the centuries

STUDYQURAN:2:142/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r10.claim: One early method divided the world into sectors oriented toward extended Kaʿbah walls; cardinal directions and markers such as summer sunrise and Canopus helped determine prayer direction.
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r10.anchor: One early method was to stand as though one were facing a wall of the Kaʿbah that was extended far enough horizontally; in this system the Islamic world was divided into geographic sectors

STUDYQURAN:2:142/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r11.claim: The great-circle route is the shortest surface path; in North America it begins northeast and curves toward southeast, while the older sector method points southeast, and both are used today.
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r11.anchor: among them the great circle, which is the shortest surface line between Makkah and any spot on the earth. In North America, for example, the great circle to Makkah begins in a northeasterly direction

STUDYQURAN:2:142/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r12.claim: Another method keeps a constant compass bearing, or rhumb line, toward Makkah.
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r12.anchor: Another method is to face the direction that, if one kept a constant compass bearing or “rhumb line,” would bring one to Makkah.

STUDYQURAN:2:142/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r13.claim: Older mosques could point in different directions because of nonmathematical local methods; Islamic mathematics later used instruments and sometimes prompted wall adjustments.
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r13.anchor: In some old Islamic cities the qiblah of various mosques was not always uniformly oriented, because it was calculated using the nonmathematical means available to their inhabitants.

STUDYQURAN:2:142/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r14.speaker: aḥādith
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r14.claim: A hadith says the area between East and West is a qiblah; it is read as allowing latitude on precision when calculation or local conditions make exact direction difficult or impossible.
STUDYQURAN:2:142/r14.anchor: Aḥadith states, “Whatever is between the east and the west is a qiblah” (IK, Q), which has been interpreted as providing a certain latitude when it comes to matters of exact direction,

TAB-FULL:v2p615/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p615/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p615/r1.claim: The ‘foolish’ are ignorant Jews and hypocrites: Jewish leaders reject the truth and their ignorant people arrogantly refuse Muhammad because he is Arab, while hypocrites are perplexed and dull.
TAB-FULL:v2p615/r1.anchor: سيقول الجهال من الناس وهم اليهود، وأهل النفاق وإنما سماهم الله عز وجل سفهاء، لأنهم سفهوا الحق

TAB-FULL:v2p615/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p615/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v2p615/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies the people who ask why the qibla changed as Jews speaking when the community left Jerusalem.
TAB-FULL:v2p615/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله عز وجل: " {سيقول السفهاء} [البقرة: 142] من الناس ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم قال: اليهود تقوله حين ترك بيت المقدس

TAB-FULL:v2p615/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p615/r3.speaker: البراء
TAB-FULL:v2p615/r3.claim: Al-Baraʾ identifies the foolish people who objected to the qibla change as Jews; another report calls them People of the Book.
TAB-FULL:v2p615/r3.anchor: عن البراء، " {سيقول السفهاء من الناس} [البقرة: 142] قال: اليهود

TAB-FULL:v2p615/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p615/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p615/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people called foolish were Jews.
TAB-FULL:v2p615/r4.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس، قال: «اليهود»

TAB-FULL:v2p615/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p615/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v2p615/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse was revealed about hypocrites.
TAB-FULL:v2p615/r5.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " نزلت {سيقول السفهاء من الناس} [البقرة: 142] في المنافقين

TAB-FULL:v2p617/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p617/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p617/r1.claim: Mā wallāhum asks what turned them away; the verb describes turning one’s face and presenting one’s back to something.
TAB-FULL:v2p617/r1.anchor: أي شيء حول وجوه هؤلاء فصرفها عن الموضع الذي كانوا يستقبلونه بوجوههم في صلاتهم؟

TAB-FULL:v2p617/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p617/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p617/r2.claim: Qibla is the direction or object facing one’s face, a noun on the faʿla pattern like jalsa and qaʿda.
TAB-FULL:v2p617/r2.anchor: فإن قبلة كل شيء ما قابل وجهه، وإنما هي «فعلة» بمنزلة الجلسة والقعدة

TAB-FULL:v2p617/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p617/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p617/r3.claim: The question asks why believers turned from the Jewish qibla at Jerusalem toward the Sacred Mosque; God tells Muhammad to answer that east and west belong to Him and He guides whom He wills.
TAB-FULL:v2p617/r3.anchor: إذا حولتم وجوهكم عن قبلة اليهود التي كانت لكم قبلة قبل أمري إياكم بتحويل وجوهكم عنها شطر المسجد الحرام

TAB-FULL:v2p617/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p617/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p617/r4.claim: The context is that Muhammad prayed toward Jerusalem for a period before God willed to turn his and his companions’ qibla toward the Kaaba.
TAB-FULL:v2p617/r4.anchor: وكان سبب ذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى نحو بيت المقدس مدة سنذكر مبلغها فيما بعد إن شاء الله تعالى ثم أراد الله تعالى صرف قبلة نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى المسجد الحرام

TAB-FULL:v2p619/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p619/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p619/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that in Rajab, 17 months after the Hijra, Jewish leaders including Rifaʿa, Qardam, Kaʿb al-Ashraf, Nafiʿ, Hajjaj, Rabiʿ, and Kinana challenged Muhammad’s turn from Syria to the Kaaba and urged him back to tempt him; 2:142–143 was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v2p619/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " لما صرفت القبلة عن الشام، إلى الكعبة، وصرفت في رجب على رأس سبعة عشر شهرا

TAB-FULL:v2p619/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p619/r2.speaker: البراء
TAB-FULL:v2p619/r2.claim: Al-Baraʾ reports a 17-month Jerusalem period; after two rakʿas, worshippers learned of the change and completed prayer facing the Kaaba, which Muhammad had hoped to face.
TAB-FULL:v2p619/r2.anchor: قال البراء، " صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نحو بيت المقدس سبعة عشر شهرا، وكان يشتهي أن يصرف إلى الكعبة

TAB-FULL:v2p619/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p619/r3.speaker: أبو كريب
TAB-FULL:v2p619/r3.claim: Abu Kurayb was asked whether Abu Ishaq was in the chain for the report, and the narrator remained silent; al-Tabari states no grade.
TAB-FULL:v2p619/r3.anchor: قال أبو كريب: فقيل له: فيه أبو إسحاق؟ فسكت

TAB-FULL:v2p621/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p621/r1.speaker: البراء بن عازب
TAB-FULL:v2p621/r1.claim: Al-Baraʾ ibn ʿAzib reports that the Jerusalem prayer lasted 16 or 17 months, with Sufyan unsure of the number, before the turn to the Kaaba.
TAB-FULL:v2p621/r1.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب، قال: «صليت مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نحو بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا أو سبعة عشر شهرا» شك سفيان ثم صرفنا إلى الكعبة

TAB-FULL:v2p621/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p621/r2.speaker: البراء
TAB-FULL:v2p621/r2.claim: Al-Baraʾ says the period was 16 months; after an afternoon prayer, a messenger announced the change, worshippers turned while bowing, and Jews who had welcomed Muhammad’s Jerusalem prayer rejected the Kaaba direction.
TAB-FULL:v2p621/r2.anchor: عن البراء، " أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان أول ما قدم المدينة نزل على أجداده أو أخواله من الأنصار، وأنه صلى قبل بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا

TAB-FULL:v2p621/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p621/r3.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
TAB-FULL:v2p621/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says Muhammad prayed toward Jerusalem for 16 months and turned toward the Kaaba two months before Badr.
TAB-FULL:v2p621/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب، قال: «صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نحو بيت المقدس بعد أن قدم المدينة ستة عشر شهرا، ثم وجه نحو الكعبة قبل بدر، بشهرين»

TAB-FULL:v2p621/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p621/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v2p621/r4.claim: Anas reports a period of nine or ten months; Muhammad turned toward the Kaaba during the noon prayer after its first two rakʿas, prompting the question about the former qibla.
TAB-FULL:v2p621/r4.anchor: ثنا أنس بن مالك، قال: " صلى نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نحو بيت المقدس تسعة أشهر أو عشرة أشهر

TAB-FULL:v2p621/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p621/r5.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
TAB-FULL:v2p621/r5.claim: Muʿadh ibn Jabal reports that Muhammad prayed toward Jerusalem for thirteen months after arriving in Medina.
TAB-FULL:v2p621/r5.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل: «أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قدم المدينة، فصلى نحو بيت المقدس ثلاثة عشر شهرا»

TAB-FULL:v2p623/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r1.speaker: عكرمة والحسن البصري
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r1.claim: Ikrima and al-Hasan say Muhammad chose Jerusalem, the Jews’ qibla, for 17 months to win them over and attract unschooled Arabs; they call qibla the first abrogated matter and cite 2:115.
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة، وعن يزيد النحوي، عن عكرمة، والحسن البصري، قالا: " أول ما نسخ من القرآن القبلة، وذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يستقبل صخرة بيت المقدس

TAB-FULL:v2p623/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r2.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r2.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the qibla meant in ‘the qibla they had been on’ was Jerusalem.
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r2.anchor: عن الربيع، في قوله: " {سيقول السفهاء من الناس ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها} [البقرة: 142] يعنون بيت المقدس

TAB-FULL:v2p623/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya says God gave the Prophet a choice, and he chose Jerusalem to reconcile the People of Scripture; after 16 months, he prayed and looked toward heaven until God directed him to the Sacred House.
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r3.anchor: قال الربيع، قال أبو العالية، «إن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خير أن يوجه وجهه حيث شاء، فاختار بيت المقدس لكي يتألف أهل الكتاب

TAB-FULL:v2p623/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas gives the alternative that God commanded Jerusalem after the Hijra because most Medinans were Jews; they rejoiced, while Muhammad loved Abraham’s qibla and looked heavenward until 2:144 redirected him, provoking Jewish doubt.
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " لما هاجر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى المدينة، وكان أكثر أهلها اليهود، أمره الله أن يستقبل بيت المقدس

TAB-FULL:v2p625/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p625/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p625/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jews asked Muhammad to return to his former qibla, promising to follow and believe, in an attempt to tempt him away from his religion.
TAB-FULL:v2p625/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " قال ذلك قوم من اليهود للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقالوا له: ارجع إلى قبلتك التي كنت عليها نتبعك ونصدقك

TAB-FULL:v2p625/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p625/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p625/r2.claim: The alternative report from Ibn Abbas through Ali ibn Abi Talha is that God had commanded Jerusalem as the qibla after the migration.
TAB-FULL:v2p625/r2.anchor: والقول الآخر: ما ذكرت من حديث علي بن أبي طلحة عنه الذي مضى قبل

TAB-FULL:v2p625/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p625/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p625/r3.claim: Qatada says the Ansar prayed toward Jerusalem for two years before the Hijra and Muhammad for 16 months after it; some said he longed for his birthplace, and God answered that He owns both directions and guides whom He wills.
TAB-FULL:v2p625/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {سيقول السفهاء من الناس ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها} [البقرة: 142] " قال: " صلت الأنصار نحو بيت المقدس حولين

TAB-FULL:v2p625/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p625/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v2p625/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says hypocrites mocked the community for leaving a qibla they had followed for a time; the verse was revealed concerning their objection.
TAB-FULL:v2p625/r4.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " لما وجه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل المسجد الحرام، اختلف الناس فيها، فكانوا أصنافا، فقال المنافقون

TAB-FULL:v2p625#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p625#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p625#2/r1.claim: God owns the east, west, and all the world between the sun’s farthest rising and setting points.
TAB-FULL:v2p625#2/r1.anchor: والمغرب؛ يعني بذلك ملك ما بين قطري مشرق الشمس، وقطري مغربها، وما بينهما من العالم

TAB-FULL:v2p625#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p625#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p625#2/r2.claim: God steadies and guides whom He wills to Abraham’s straight qibla, and leaves astray whom He wills; Tabari applies this to guidance of believers and the loss of Jews, hypocrites, and polytheists.
TAB-FULL:v2p625#2/r2.anchor: يهدي من يشاء من خلقه فيسدده، ويوفقه إلى الطريق القويم، وهو الصراط المستقيم. ويعني بذلك إلى قبلة إبراهيم

TAB-FULL:v2p625#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p625#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p625#2/r3.claim: Tabari says God guided Muslims toward Abraham’s qibla at the Sacred Mosque and withheld that guidance from Jews, hypocrites, and polytheists.
TAB-FULL:v2p625#2/r3.anchor: قل: يا محمد إن الله هدانا بالتوجه شطر المسجد الحرام لقبلة إبراهيم وأضلكم أيها اليهود، والمنافقون، وجماعة الشرك بالله

TABATABAI:2:142/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142/r1.claim: The verses form a coherent sequence announcing the Kaaba as the Muslims' qibla; reports alleging disorder or abrogation conflict with the apparent text and should not be accepted.
TABATABAI:2:142/r1.anchor: وهي تنبىء عن جعل الكعبة قبلة للمسلمين فلا يصغى إلى قول من يقول إن فيها تقدما وتأخرا أو إن فيها ناسخا ومنسوخا،

TABATABAI:2:142/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142/r2.claim: The announced objection comes from Jews defending Jerusalem and pagan Arabs watching for disputes; Abraham and Ishmael's honor, prayers, construction of the House, and its purification prepare the answer.
TABATABAI:2:142/r2.anchor: وقد مهد لذلك أولا بما ذكره الله تعالى من قصص إبراهيم عليه السلام وأنواع كرامته على الله سبحانه وكرامة ابنه إسماعيل ودعوتهما للكعبة ومكة

TABATABAI:2:142/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142/r3.claim: Changing the qibla after the migration was a major religious event and foundational legislation; Jews resisted because it removed one of their chief religious distinctions and the deference of others.
TABATABAI:2:142/r3.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن تحويل القبلة من بيت المقدس إلى الكعبة من أعظم الحوادث الدينية وأهم التشريعات التي قوبل به الناس بعد هجرة النبي إلى المدينة،

TABATABAI:2:142/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142/r4.claim: A common qibla strongly unites Muslims' outward worship and inward community, and its visible effect on Jews and Arab polytheists exceeds that of purification or supplication.
TABATABAI:2:142/r4.anchor: لجمعه وجوههم في عباداتهم ومناسكهم الدينية إلى نقطة واحدة يخلصهم من تفرق الوجوه في الظاهر وشتات الكلمة في الباطن

TABATABAI:2:142/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142/r5.claim: The author portrays the Jews as giving little reality to the unseen beyond nature: they accept non-sensory rulings but resist God's commands tied to visible acts and material life.
TABATABAI:2:142/r5.anchor: فقد كانوا أمة لا يرون لغير المحسوس من عالم الطبيعة أصالة ولا لغير الحس وقعا،

TABATABAI:2:142/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142/r6.claim: The anticipated objection asks how God could replace Jerusalem, which He had made qibla for earlier prophets, with a less honored House; Jews rejected abrogation, while a change without divine order would be deviation.
TABATABAI:2:142/r6.anchor: فإن كان بأمر من الله فإن الله هو الذي جعل بيت المقدس قبلة فكيف ينقض حكمه وينسخ ما شرعه،

TABATABAI:2:142-144/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r1.claim: No building, stone, or direction has an intrinsic claim to be the qibla; all places and directions belong equally to God, who legislates as He wills to guide people toward their individual and collective perfection.
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r1.anchor: بل جميع الأجسام والأبنية وجميع الجهات التي يمكن أن يتوجه إليه الإنسان في أنها لا تقتضي حكما ولا يستوجب تشريعا على السواء وكلها لله

TABATABAI:2:142-144/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r2.claim: The 'foolish' are Jews and Arab polytheists, whose unsound nature and unstable judgment distort their view of religious law; foolishness means defective reason and unsettled judgment.
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r2.anchor: أراد بهم اليهود والمشركين من العرب ولذلك عبر عنهم بالناس وإنما سفههم لعدم استقامة فطرتهم وثقوب رأيهم في أمر التشريع،

TABATABAI:2:142-144/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r3.claim: Tawliyat toward a place means putting it before one's face, while turning away means turning one's face from it, as in turning one's back.
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r3.anchor: تولية الشيء أو المكان جعله قدام الوجه وأمامه كالاستقبال،

TABATABAI:2:142-144/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r4.claim: The earlier qibla was Jerusalem, which the Prophet and Muslims faced in Mecca and for several months after migrating to Medina; attributing it to Muslims rather than the older Jewish users heightens the objection.
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r4.anchor: وهو بيت المقدس الذي كان يصلي إليه النبي والمسلمون أيام إقامته بمكة وعدة شهور بعد هجرته إلى المدينة

TABATABAI:2:142-144/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r5.claim: The wording asks what turned them from their qibla instead of asking why the Prophet and Muslims left the Jews' qibla, since the latter would make the answer obvious and weaken the surprise.
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r5.anchor: فلو قيل ما ولى النبي والمسلمين عن قبلة اليهود لم يكن التعجب واقعا موقعه وكان الجواب عنه ظاهرا لكل سامع

TABATABAI:2:142-144/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r6.claim: East and west stand for all directions: they are relative orientations fixed by the rising and setting of the sun or stars and cover the earth except for the imagined true north and south poles.
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r6.anchor: والمشرق والمغرب جهتان إضافيتان تتعينان بشروق الشمس أو النجوم وغروبهما، يعمان جميع نقاط الأرض

TABATABAI:2:142-144/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r7.claim: The path is indefinite because the straight path varies according to each community's readiness for guidance toward perfection and happiness.
TABATABAI:2:142-144/r7.anchor: تنكير الصراط لأن الصراط يختلف باختلاف الأمم في استعداداتها للهداية إلى الكمال والسعادة.

TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r1.claim: Because God transcends material perception, inward orientation must be represented in bodily forms that match its meaning; orientation gives worship its life.
TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r1.anchor: أن التوجه إلى المعبود، واستقباله من العبد في عبوديته روح عبادته

TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r2.claim: Pagans, star worshippers, and others physically faced their deities; Islam instead directs worship toward the Kaaba, continuing the prophetic religions.
TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r2.anchor: وقد كانت الوثنيون وعبدة الكواكب وسائر الأجسام من الإنسان وغيره يستقبلون معبوداتهم وآلهتهم ويتوجهون إليهم بالأبدان

TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r3.claim: Islam makes the Kaaba the prayer direction for Muslims everywhere and regulates when people should face it or turn away from it.
TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r3.anchor: وضع الكعبة قبلة، وأمر باستقبالها في الصلاة التي لا يعذر فيها مسلم أينما كان من أقطار الأرض وآفاقها، ونهى عن استقبالها واستدبارها في حالات

TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r4.claim: The qibla preserves a person's continual attention to God through ordinary life, worship, and even the most private states.
TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r4.anchor: فاحتفظ على قلب الإنسان بالتوجه إلى بيت الله، وأن لا ينسى ربه في خلوته وجلوته، وقيامه وقعوده

TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r5.claim: A single direction unites Muslims across times and places, expressing shared thought and binding their community despite later sectarian divisions.
TABATABAI:2:142-151#10/r5.anchor: فقد جمع الناس على اختلاف أزمنتهم وأمكنتهم على التوجه إلى نقطة واحدة، يمثل بذلك وحدتهم الفكرية وارتباط جامعتهم

TABATABAI:2:153-157#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#8/r1.claim: The command to face the qibla calls for determination and steadiness, justified by preventing people from having an argument against the believers.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#8/r1.anchor: وحيثما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره لئلا يكون للناس عليكم حجة

ZAJJAJ:v1p218/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p218/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p218/r4.claim: The “foolish people” who question the change of qibla are identified in two views as either the Meccan unbelievers or the Jews.
ZAJJAJ:v1p218/r4.anchor: كفار أهل مكة، وقيل يعني به: إليهود والسفهاء واحدهم سفيه،

ZAJJAJ:v1p218/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p218/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p218/r5.claim: “Sufahāʾ” is the plural of “safīh,” like “shuhadāʾ” from “shahīd” and “ʿulamāʾ” from “ʿalīm.”
ZAJJAJ:v1p218/r5.anchor: والسفهاء واحدهم سفيه، - مثل شهيد وشهداء، وعليم وعلماء.

ZAJJAJ:v1p218#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p218#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p218#2/r1.claim: “Mā wallāhum” asks what turned them away from their previous qibla, the direction toward Jerusalem.
ZAJJAJ:v1p218#2/r1.anchor: معنى؛ (ما ولاهم): ما عدلهم عنها يعني قبلة بيت المقدس.

ZAJJAJ:v1p218#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p218#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p218#2/r2.claim: The Prophet was ordered to face Jerusalem because Meccans were accustomed to pilgrimage to the Kaʿba; God tested the community with an unfamiliar direction to distinguish those who followed the Messenger.
ZAJJAJ:v1p218#2/r2.anchor: لأن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان أمر بالصلاة إلى بيت المقدس، لأن مكة وبيت الله الحرام كانت العرب آلفة لحجه

ZAJJAJ:v1p218#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p218#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p218#2/r3.claim: Wherever God commands prayer and worship belongs to Him; the author says He knows and is there, citing verses about God in heaven and earth, with people, and as the fourth of three in private conversation.
ZAJJAJ:v1p218#2/r3.anchor: معناه حيث أمر الله أن يصلى ويتعبد، فهو له، وعالم به، وهو فيه كما قال: (وهو الله في السماوات وفي الأرض يعلم سركم

ZAJJAJ:v1p219/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p219/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p219/r1.claim: The “straight path” means a straight road in accordance with what God approves.
ZAJJAJ:v1p219/r1.anchor: معناه: طريق مستقيم كما يحب الله.

TABRISI:2:142/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:142/r1.claim: Safīh, jāhil, and ghabī are near-synonyms: foolish, ignorant, and dull.

TABRISI:2:142/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:142/r2.claim: Wallāhu ʿan means he turned someone away; the root walī is closeness and succession without a gap, and the directional forms indicate turning toward versus away.
TABRISI:2:142/r2.anchor: واشتقاقه من الولي وهو القرب وهو حصول الثاني بعد الأول من غير فصل

TABRISI:2:142/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:142/r3.claim: Qibla first meant the posture or direction in which one thing faces another, then became the name for the direction faced in prayer.
TABRISI:2:142/r3.anchor: ثم صار علما على الجهة التي تستقبل في الصلاة

TABRISI:2:142/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:142/r4.claim: In the syntax, min al-nās is a circumstantial phrase modifying al-sufahāʾ; mā is an interrogative subject, wallāhum its predicate, and ʿan qiblatihim the complement of wallā.
TABRISI:2:142/r4.anchor: من الناس في محل النصب حال من السفهاء وما استفهام وهو مبتدأ وولاهم خبره

TABRISI:2:142/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:142/r5.claim: The passage turns to those who criticized Muslims for shifting from Jerusalem to the Kaaba.
TABRISI:2:142/r5.anchor: ثم ذكر سبحانه الذين عابوا المسلمين بالانصراف عن قبلة بيت المقدس إلى الكعبة

TABRISI:2:142/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:142/r6.claim: The fools are ignorant people among humanity, namely unbelievers.
TABRISI:2:142/r6.anchor: أي سوف يقول الجهال وهم الكفار الذين هم بعض الناس

TABRISI:2:142/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:142/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and others identify the critics as Jews.
TABRISI:2:142/r7.anchor: اختلف في الذين قالوا ذلك فقال ابن عباس وغيره هم اليهود

TABRISI:2:142/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r8.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:142/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says the critics were Arab polytheists, who accused Muhammad of leaving his fathers' qibla and then returning to it, and taunted him to return to their religion.

TABRISI:2:142/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r9.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:2:142/r9.claim: Al-Suddi says hypocrites said it to mock Islam.
TABRISI:2:142/r9.anchor: وقال السدي هم المنافقون قالوا ذلك استهزاء بالإسلام

TABRISI:2:142/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:142/r10.claim: One motive was to object to abrogation of the former qibla.
TABRISI:2:142/r10.anchor: فقيل إنهم قالوا على وجه الإنكار للنسخ عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:2:142/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
