TABRISI:2:142/r11.claim: Another report says critics promised to follow and believe Muhammad if he returned to their qibla, intending to tempt him away.
TABRISI:2:142/r11.anchor: يا محمد ما ولاك عن قبلتك التي كنت عليها ارجع إلى قبلتنا نتبعك ونؤمن بك

TABRISI:2:142/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:142/r12.claim: A further view says Arab polytheists made the taunt to suggest that truth lay with their own practice.
TABRISI:2:142/r12.anchor: وقيل إنما قاله مشركو العرب ليوهموا أن الحق ما هم عليه

TABRISI:2:142/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:142/r13.claim: One explanation for the qibla change is that God knew it would alter what served people's interests.
TABRISI:2:142/r13.anchor: أنه لما علم الله تعالى في ذلك من تغير المصلحة

TABRISI:2:142/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:142/r14.claim: Another explanation is the verse's test: in Mecca facing Jerusalem distinguished Muslims from Kaaba-facing polytheists; in Medina facing the Kaaba distinguished them from Jews facing Jerusalem.
TABRISI:2:142/r14.anchor: لأنهم كانوا بمكة أمروا أن يتوجهوا إلى بيت المقدس ليتميزوا من المشركين

TABRISI:2:142/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:142/r15.claim: God owns both east and west and directs them as wisdom requires, answering those who objected to leaving Jerusalem.
TABRISI:2:142/r15.anchor: المشرق والمغرب ملك الله سبحانه يتصرف فيهما كيف شاء على ما تقتضيه حكمته

TABRISI:2:142/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:142/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:142/r16.claim: This refutes the claim that the Holy Land is more deserving as the prayer direction because prophets lived there: all places belong to God, who sanctifies whichever He wills at each time for people's interests.
TABRISI:2:142/r16.anchor: فرد الله سبحانه عليهم بأن المواطن كلها لله يشرف منها ما يشاء في كل زمان

THALABI:v2p7#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p7#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p7#2/r1.claim: Al-sufahāʾ means the ignorant; mā wallāhum asks who turned and redirected them.
THALABI:v2p7#2/r1.anchor: سيقول السفهاء الجهال. من الناس ما ولاهم صرفهم وحولهم

THALABI:v2p7#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p7#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p7#2/r2.anchor: عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها من بيت المقدس

THALABI:v2p7#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p7#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p7#2/r3.claim: The verse was revealed after Jews, Meccan idolaters, and Medinan hypocrites criticized the qibla change; Meccan pagans claimed Muḥammad was wavering, longing for his birthplace and his fathers’ birthplace, and would soon return to their religion.
THALABI:v2p7#2/r3.anchor: نزلت في اليهود ومشركي العرب بمكة ومنافقي المدينة طعنوا في تحويل القبلة

THALABI:v2p7#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p7#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p7#2/r4.claim: God owns east and west, and His creatures are servants whom He redirects as He wills.
THALABI:v2p7#2/r4.anchor: قال الله قل لله المشرق والمغرب ملكا والخلق عبيده يحولهم كيف شاء

ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r1.claim: Before the qiblah revelation, the Prophet and community prayed toward the Ka'bah without a specific command; it was regarded as the first temple devoted to the One God despite its idols.
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r1.anchor: used to turn in prayer towards the Ka'bah. This was not prompted by any specific revelation

ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r2.claim: Because the Prophet recognized Jerusalem's sanctity, he usually stood by the Ka'bah's southern wall, facing north toward both holy centers.
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r2.anchor: the Prophet prayed, as a rule, before the southern wall of the Ka'bah, towards the north, so as to face both the Ka'bah and Jerusalem

ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r3.claim: After the move to Medina he prayed toward Jerusalem alone; about sixteen months later revelation definitively made the Ka'bah the Qur'an community's qiblah.
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r3.anchor: definitively established the Ka'bah as the qiblah of the followers of the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r4.claim: Medina's Jews were displeased when Muslims abandoned Jerusalem, whose direction had pleased them.
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r4.anchor: it is to them that the opening sentence of this passage refers

ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r5.claim: Historically, no divine qiblah command changed: no ordinance on direction of prayer existed before 2:142-150 was revealed.
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r5.anchor: there had simply been no ordinance whatever in this respect before verses 142-150 were revealed

ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r6.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r6.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r6.claim: The passage connects to the preceding discussion of Abraham because he erected the earliest temple structure later known as the Ka'bah.
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n116/r6.anchor: Abraham who erected the earliest structure of the temple which later came to be known as the Ka'bah

ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n117/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n117/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n117/r1.claim: Asad offers an alternate rendering in which God guides whoever wills to be guided onto a straight path.
ASAD-NOTES:2:142#n117/r1.anchor: Or: "He guides onto a straight way him that wills [to be guided]"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r1.claim: The verse was revealed about changing the direction of prayer to the Kaaba.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r1.anchor: - قوله تعالى {سيقول السفهاء من الناس} الآية، نزلت في تحويل القبلة إلى الكعبة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r2.claim: He identifies the ‘foolish’ people as the Jews of Medina.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: عنى بالسفهاء يهود المدينة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r3.claim: He identifies the ‘foolish’ people as the polytheists of Mecca.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r4.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r4.claim: He identifies them as Medina’s hypocrites; the polytheists said Muhammad longed for his birthplace and might return to their religion, Jews said he was confused, and hypocrites mocked the change.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: يعني منافقي المدينة، وذلك أن المشركين قالوا لما توجه النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إلى الكعبة: قد اشتاق محمد إلى مولده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r5.claim: سفهاء is the plural of سفيه, a person who lightly rushes toward what he should not.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r5.anchor: والسفهاء: جمع سفيه، وهو الخفيف إلى ما لا يجوز له أن يخف إليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r6.claim: ما ولاهم means ‘what turned them’ or ‘what diverted them.’
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p367#2/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم} أي: عدلهم وصرفهم (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368/r1.claim: Qibla means direction and is formed from مقابلة; the root sense is the state in which one thing faces another, later lexicalized as the direction faced in prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368/r1.anchor: القبلة: الوجهة، وهي الفعلة من المقابلة، والعرب تقول: ماله قبلة ولا دبرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368/r2.claim: The phrase ‘the one they had been upon’ means Jerusalem according to most exegetes; the pronoun refers to the Prophet and his companions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368/r2.anchor: يعنون: بيت المقدس، في قول أكثر المفسرين، والضمير في قبلتهم: للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأصحابه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368/r3.claim: He says it means the qibla of Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes; on their claim that Abraham faced Jerusalem, the pronoun refers to those forefathers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368/r3.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد التي كان عليها إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368/r4.claim: He prefers the first interpretation, that the qibla was Jerusalem and the pronoun refers to the Prophet and his companions, which is the exegetes’ position.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368#2/r1.claim: God owns both east and west and may command people to face whichever direction He chooses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368#2/r1.anchor: أي: له أن يأمر بالتوجه إلى أي جهة شاء (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368#2/r2.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368#2/r2.claim: One view takes ‘the east’ specifically as the Kaaba: from Medina it lies east, whereas Jerusalem lies west.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالمشرق الكعبة؛ لأن المصلي بالمدينة إذا توجه إلى الكعبة فهو متوجه إلى المشرق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368#2/r3.claim: He glosses the straight path as the straight religion: God approved the earlier qibla and this qibla for Muhammad; religion is a straight path because it leads to Paradise like a straight road reaches its destination.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p368#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إلى دين مستقيم، يريد: أني قد رضيت قبلة أولئك، ورضيت هذه القبلة لمحمد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:142-143/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:142-143/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:142-143/r1.claim: The foolish people are Meccan polytheists and Medina's Jews; their question refers to Muhammad and the believers being turned from their former qibla, the Rock.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:142-143/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:142-143/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:142-143/r2.claim: God owns east and west, directs people toward whichever direction He chooses, and guides whom He wills to an upright religion; He chose this qibla for Muhammad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:142-143/r2.anchor: يأمر بالتوجه إلى أي جهة شاء { يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم } دين مستقيم.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r1.claim: After a single interrogative, أو coordinates alternatives when the question seeks one answer naming the person or object.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r1.anchor: أيهم تضرب أو تقتل تعمل أحدهما

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r2.claim: هل differs from interrogative alif: هل does not presuppose that an action occurred, whereas alif may confront someone with a known action.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r2.anchor: ألف الاستفهام ليست بمنزلة هل أنك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r3.speaker: العرب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r3.claim: Speakers may use أم هل when the second question is a separate clause or renewed thought; others use أو هل for one continuing question.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r3.anchor: فإنما قالوه على أنه أدركه الظن بعد ما مضى صدر حديثه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r4.claim: In indirect inquiry after ما أدري or ليت شعري, هل retains its interrogative force and may coordinate alternatives with أو.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r6.claim: Poetic examples from Zuhayr, Mālik ibn al-Rayb, Zafar ibn al-Ḥārith, and ʿAlqama show هل used with أم or أو; Sībawayh reports a separate-question reading for some cases.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r6.anchor: فهذا سمعناه ممن ينشده من بني عمه

RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r1.claim: Not every essence can receive a word: essences are infinite, and what cannot be distinctly apprehended cannot be assigned a name.
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r1.anchor: لا يمكن أن تكون جميع الماهيات مسميات بالألفاظ لأن الماهيات غير متناهية وما لا نهاية له لا يكون مشعورا به على التفصيل

RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r2.claim: The more urgent a meaning is to express, the more fitting it is to coin a word for it; commands, prohibitions, generality, and particularity illustrate this need.
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r2.anchor: كل معنى كانت الحاجة إلى التعبير عنه أهم كان وضع اللفظ بإزائه أولى مثل صيغ الأوامر والنواهي والعموم والخصوص

RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r3.claim: A common word cannot name a meaning hidden from most people: common الحركة denotes bodily movement, not the obscure cause proposed by some theologians.
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r3.anchor: المعنى الذي يكون خفيا عند الجمهور يمتنع كونه مسمى باللفظ المشهور مثاله لفظة الحركة لفظة مشهورة

RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r4.claim: Accordingly, الحركة names the transition itself, while knowledge and power name being knowing and being capable, not hidden causes of those states.
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r4.anchor: الحركة اسم لنفس هذا الانتقال لا للمعنى الذي يوجب الانتقال

RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r5.claim: Meaning is the mental image intended by a speaker, not external things in themselves; external objects are meant only secondarily.
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r5.anchor: المعنى اسم للصورة الذهنية لا للموجودات الخارجية لأن المعنى عبارة عن الشيء الذي عناه العاني

RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r6.claim: The difference between plant sweetness and sugar-candy sweetness lacks a dedicated word, so it can be described only relationally; a coined term would make verbal definition possible.
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r6.anchor: حلاوة النبات وحلاوة الطبرزذ فلما لم توضع لتلك التفرقة لفظة مخصوصة لا جرم لا يمكن تعريفها باللفظ

RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r7.claim: A person cannot name a private inner state for listeners who have never conceived it; if a group first conceived that state and coined a term, they could define it verbally.
RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r7.anchor: استحال لهذا المدرك وضع لفظ لتعريفه لأن السامع ما لم يعرف المسمى أولا لم يمكنه أن يفهم

TABRISI:2:144/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144/r7.claim: Guidance means directing someone to the religion; it is called a straight path because it leads to Paradise, the destination.
TABRISI:2:144/r7.anchor: أي يدله ويرشده إلى الدين وإنما سماه الصراط لأنه طريق الجنة المؤدي إليها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī urges learning the modes of Qurʾānic address and the Sunnah's clarifications of revelation so that arbitrary, linguistically uninformed interpretations do not generate error and doubt.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r1.anchor: فعلينا أن نجتهد في تعلم ما يتوصل بتعلمه إلى معرفة ضروب خطاب الكتاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r2.claim: Early authorities encouraged Arabic because it is essential for understanding the Qurʾān, Sunnah, reports, and the unusual language in the exegesis of Companions and Successors.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r2.anchor: وقد كان الأكابر من السلف يحثون على تعلم لغة العرب، ويرغبون فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r3.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r3.claim: A report from the Prophet says a father has given his child no gift better than good manners; al-Wāḥidī states no grading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: "ما نحل والد ولده نحلة (¬4) أفضل من أدب حسن"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r4.claim: Saʿīd b. al-Musayyab reports that ʿUmar asked about takhawwuf in 16:47; a Hudhalī elder glossed it as gradual diminution and said Arab poetry attested the usage, naming Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p397/r4.anchor: وروي عن سعيد بن المسيب (¬1) أنه قال: بينا عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه على المنبر

BURHAN:v2p37/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p37/r1.speaker: أبو الحسين أحمد بن جعفر المنادى
BURHAN:v2p37/r1.claim: Al-Munādī records the two Witr qunūt surahs among material whose written recitation was lifted while its wording remained memorized; he says they were in Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's codices and were taught to him by the Prophet.
BURHAN:v2p37/r1.anchor: ذكر الإمام المحدث أبو الحسين أحمد بن جعفر ( 2 ) المنادى في كتابه الناسخ والمنسوخ

BURHAN:v2p37/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p37/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p37/r2.claim: The two Witr qunūt surahs are also called al-Khalʿ and al-Ḥafd.

BURHAN:v2p37/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p37/r3.speaker: صاحب الفنون
BURHAN:v2p37/r3.claim: The author of al-Funūn explains that lifting recitation while retaining the rule tests the community's prompt obedience based on probable evidence, like Abraham's readiness to sacrifice his son after a dream.
BURHAN:v2p37/r3.anchor: وأجاب صاحب الفنون ( 3 ) فقال إنما كان كذلك ليظهر به مقدار طاعة هذه الأمة في المسارعة

BURHAN:v2p37/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p37/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p37/r6.claim: Zarkashī adds the qibla passages as another case: the earlier-positioned prediction سيقول السفهاء is abrogated by the later-positioned command to face the Sacred Mosque.
BURHAN:v2p37/r6.anchor: قلت وذكر بعضهم موضعا آخر وهو قوله تعالى ﴿ سيقول السفهاء من الناس ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها ﴾

BURHAN:v4p280/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p280/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p280/r5.claim: Some grammarians say sin can convey continuity; in سيقول السفهاء it signals that their criticism persists, since it had already been voiced when the verse was revealed.
BURHAN:v4p280/r5.anchor: فجاءت السين اعلاما بالاستمرار لا بالاستقبال

BURHAN:v4p280/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p280/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p280/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the sin guarantees that the promised event will occur, just as it can confirm a threat.
BURHAN:v4p280/r6.anchor: افادت السين وجود الرحمة لا محالة فهي تؤكد الوعد كما تؤكد الوعيد

BURHAN:v4p280/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p280/r8.speaker: الطيبي
BURHAN:v4p280/r8.claim: Al-Ṭībī's account equating sin in affirmation with إن in negation is rejected: that would emphasize the promised event, not explain Zamakhsharī's emphasis on the promise.
BURHAN:v4p280/r8.anchor: وقال الطيبي مراد الزمخشري إن السين في الاثبات مقابلة إن في النفي وهذا مردود

BURHAN:v4p280/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p280/r10.speaker: الزمخشري وابن الخشاب وابن يعيش وابن أبان وابن بابشاذ وابن عصفور
BURHAN:v4p280/r10.claim: Zamakhsharī and several grammarians hold that سوف signals a longer delay than sin; the nearby سيقول contrasts with وسوف تسألون.
BURHAN:v4p280/r10.anchor: حرف يدل على التأخير والتنفيس وزمانه ابعد من زمان السين

ITQAN:v3p214/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p214/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p214/r2.claim: ‘What turned them away from their former qibla?’ may express astonishment or be a genuine question.
ITQAN:v3p214/r2.anchor: ويحتمل التعجب والاستفهام الحقيقي ﴿ ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم ﴾

ITQAN:v1p225/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p225/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p225/r2.claim: An absolute stop permits a fresh beginning after self-contained speech, including an initial noun or independent verb; سيقول السفهاء is an example of the latter.
ITQAN:v1p225/r2.anchor: والفعل المستأنف نحو ﴿ يعبدونني لا يشركون بي شيئا ﴾ و ﴿ سيقول السفهاء ﴾

ITQAN:v1p225/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p225/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p225/r3.claim: Other absolute-stop settings include an omitted object, a condition, an explicit or implicit question, and a negation, when they are not quoted speech continuing a prior statement.
ITQAN:v1p225/r3.anchor: ومفعول المحذوف نحو ﴿ وعد الله ﴾ ﴿ سنة الله ﴾ والشرط نحو ﴿ من يشإ الله يضلله ﴾

ITQAN:v1p225/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p225/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p225/r7.claim: Stopping before a conditional's consequence, or between a subject and its predicate, is impermissible.
ITQAN:v1p225/r7.anchor: وأما ما لا يجوز الوقف عليه فكالشرط دون جزائه والمبتدأ دون خبره

ITQAN:v1p225/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p225/r8.speaker: غيره
ITQAN:v1p225/r8.claim: Another scholar divides stops into eight kinds: complete and near-complete, deficient and near-deficient, good and near-good, and ugly and near-ugly.
ITQAN:v1p225/r8.anchor: وقال غيره الوقف في التنزيل على ثمانية أضرب تام وشبيه به وناقص وشبيه به

ITQAN:v1p225/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p225/r9.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p225/r9.claim: Ibn al-Jazari finds the usual stop categories unbounded and proposes voluntary versus forced stops; a complete utterance allows choice, and a complete stop has no lexical or semantic tie to what follows.
ITQAN:v1p225/r9.anchor: وقال ابن الجزري أكثر ما ذكر الناس في أقسام الوقف غير منضبط ولا منحصر وأقرب ما قلته في ضبطه إن الوقف ينقسم إلى اختياري واضطراري

ITQAN:v2p474#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p474#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p474#2/r1.claim: The particle سـ attaches only to an affirmative, ungoverned finite imperfect, makes it future, and narrows the future interval relative to سوف; grammarians call it a particle of temporal expansion.
ITQAN:v2p474#2/r1.anchor: حرف يختص بالمضارع ويخلصه للاستقبال وينزل منه منزلة الجزء فلذا لم تعمل فيه

ITQAN:v2p474#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p474#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v2p474#2/r2.claim: Some say سـ signals continuity rather than futurity in examples such as سيقول السفهاء, since the words had already been uttered before the verse descended.
ITQAN:v2p474#2/r2.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أنها قد تأتي للاستمرار لا للاستقبال كقوله تعالى ﴿ ستجدون آخرين ﴾ الآية ﴿ سيقول السفهاء ﴾

ITQAN:v2p474#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p474#2/r3.speaker: ابن هشام
ITQAN:v2p474#2/r3.claim: Ibn Hisham rejects the continuity reading: grammarians do not recognize it, continuity comes from the imperfect, and سـ retains its future sense because continuity is future-oriented.
ITQAN:v2p474#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن هشام وهذا لا يعرفه النحويون بل الاستمرار مستفاد من المضارع والسين باقية على الاستقبال

ITQAN:v2p474#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p474#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v2p474#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says سـ with a desirable or undesirable act assures that it will occur; al-Suyuti says it emphasizes a promise or threat by promising its occurrence.
ITQAN:v2p474#2/r4.anchor: وزعم الزمخشري أنها إذا دخلت على فعل محبوب أو مكروه أفادت أنه واقع لا محالة

ITQAN:v4p395/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p395/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p395/r1.claim: The people called foolish in 2:142 are identified as Rifa'a ibn Qays, Qardam ibn Amr, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, Rafi ibn Harmala, al-Hajjaj ibn Amr, and al-Rabi ibn Abi al-Huqayq.
ITQAN:v4p395/r1.anchor: ﴿ سيقول السفهاء ﴾ سمي منهم رفاعة بن قيس وقردم بن عمر وكعب بن الأشرف ورافع بن حرملة

ITQAN:v1p145/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p145/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p145/r1.claim: The Qur'an is called al-mutashabih because its parts resemble one another in beauty and truth.
ITQAN:v1p145/r1.anchor: وأما المتشابه فلأنه يشبه بعضه بعضا في الحسن والصدق

ITQAN:v1p145/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p145/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p145/r2.claim: The Qur'an is called al-ruh because it gives life to hearts and souls.
ITQAN:v1p145/r2.anchor: وأما الروح فلأنه تحيا به القلوب والأنفس

ITQAN:v1p145/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p145/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p145/r3.claim: The Qur'an is called al-majid because of its nobility.

ITQAN:v1p145/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p145/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p145/r4.claim: The Qur'an is called al-aziz because anyone who seeks to rival it is unable to do so.
ITQAN:v1p145/r4.anchor: وأما العزيز فلأنه يعز على من يروم معارضته

ITQAN:v1p95/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p95/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p95/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after the Hijra the Prophet faced Jerusalem for thirteen months at God's command, though he longed for Abraham's qibla; after the qibla changed, Jewish critics asked what had turned him from his former direction, and 2:142 answered them.
ITQAN:v1p95/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما هاجر إلى المدينة أمره الله أن يستقبل بيت المقدس ففرحت اليهود

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p270/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p270/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p270/r1.claim: Bashshār's claim that the sun visited while never leaving its orbit makes the image a claim that the actual celestial sun came down.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p270/r1.anchor: فقوله ولم تك تبرح الفلكا يريك أنه ادعى الشمس نفسها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p270/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p270/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p270/r2.claim: Ashjaʿ's shift from the definite sun to an indefinite one weakens the literal fantasy; al-Jurjānī proposes reading it as a sunny day, like everyday uses of indefinite sun and moon, while noting the tension this creates for the east-west conceit.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p270/r2.anchor: وأظن الوجه فيه أن تتأول تنكيره للشمس في الثاني على قولهم خرجنا في شمس حارة يريدون في يوم كان للشمس فيه حرارة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p181/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p181/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p181/r1.claim: In “they deceive God / God deceives them” and “they schemed / God schemed,” both clauses are God's report, unlike quoted speech followed by God's separate assertion.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p181/r1.anchor: لأن الأول من الكلامين فيهما كالثاني في أنه خبر من الله تعالى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p343#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p343#2/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p343#2/r1.claim: Jurjānī urges readers to compare their former repetition of unexplained expressions with their new ability to understand verbal composition and explain eloquent speakers' aims.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p343#2/r1.anchor: قصاراك أن تكرر ألفاظا لا تعرف لشيء منها تفسيرا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the linguistic root of foolishness is lightness of judgment; a thin, worn garment can also be called safih.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج : ( 69 / ب ) أصل السفه في اللغة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r2.claim: Ibn Faris uses the verb for wind bending trees; Dhu al-Rumma's poem uses تسفهت to describe the wind's effect on the tops of trees.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r2.anchor: وقال ابن فارس : يقال تسفهت الريح [ الشجر ]

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r3.speaker: ذو الرمة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r3.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's line is evidence for تسفهت meaning that the breeze swayed the tree tops.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r3.anchor: فمادت كما مادت رماح تسفهت … أعاليها مر الرياح النواسم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r4.claim: One Qur'anic sense is ignorant people, as in the taunt asking whether the believers should believe like fools.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r4.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن السفهاء في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r5.claim: The people called fools in this qibla verse are identified as Jews; another view says they are hypocrites.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r5.anchor: والثاني : اليهود . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r6.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r6.claim: An alternative identification of the fools who question the change of qibla is the hypocrites.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r7.claim: In the verse about property guardianship, al-sufaha' refers to women and children.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r7.anchor: والثالث : النساء والصبيان . ومنه قوله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r8.claim: A fourth sense is ruin: the one who turns away from Abraham's religion has ruined himself.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p350/r8.anchor: والرابع : السفه الهلاك . ومنه قوله تعالى

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r9.claim: The extended, repetitive qibla passage runs from the fools' objection and the trial of the change through the command to face Mecca and the Book-holders' refusal; its length suits the explicit pronoun.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r9.anchor: فأنت ترى أنه أطال القول ههنا، فكان المناسب أن يطيل بذكر الضيمر أيضاً وهو المناسب لإطالة السياق

NASHR:v1p491/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p491/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p491/r1.claim: For يشاء إلى, the allowed connected readings are full realization, between-between easing, or pure yāʾ; the same three apply in reverse order to في الأرض أمما.
NASHR:v1p491/r1.anchor: وفيه الثلاثة الجائزة لباقي القراءة وصلا وهي: التحقيق مذهب الجمهور، وبين بين على مذهب أكثر العراقيين، والياء المحضة

DURR-FULL:v1p344/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p344/r7.speaker: البراء
DURR-FULL:v1p344/r7.claim: Al-Barāʾ identifies the fools who questioned the change as Jews.
DURR-FULL:v1p344/r7.anchor: عن البراء في قوله {سيقول السفهاء من الناس} قال: اليهود

DURR-FULL:v1p346/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r5.claim: Qatāda says God guides whom He wills to the straight path; believers worried about their earlier prayers, so God revealed in 2:143 that He would not let their faith go to waste.
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r5.anchor: قال الله عز وجل {قل لله المشرق والمغرب يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم} وقال أناس من [] أناس: لقد صرفت القبلة إلى البيت الحرام

DURR-FULL:v1p346/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r6.claim: Qatāda says God tests His servants through successive commands to distinguish obedience from disobedience; each counts among degrees of faith, sincerity, and submission to God’s decree.
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r6.anchor: وقد يبتلي الله عباده بما شاء من أمره الأمر بعد الأمر ليعلم من يطيعه ممن يعصيه وكل ذلك مقبول في درجات في الإيمان بالله والاخلاص والتسليم لقضاء الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r1.claim: The placement initially seems puzzling: this verse predicts a future criticism, which one would expect after the change of prayer direction and its abrogating verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r1.anchor: قد خفي موقع هذه الآية من الآي التي بعدها لأن الظاهر منها أنها إخبار عن أمر يقع في المستقبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r2.claim: The apparent referent of the changed qibla is the former direction, Jerusalem or the east, which was the Jews’ qibla; earlier exegetes did not adequately resolve the placement or context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالقبلة المحولة القبلة المنسوخة وهي استقبال بيت المقدس أعني الشرق وهي قبلة اليهود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur’s preferred context is that earlier praise of Abraham, his religion, and the Kaaba prompts the polytheists to ask why Muhammad turned from the Kaaba to Jerusalem despite claiming Abraham’s religion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r3.anchor: والذي استقر عليه فهمي أن مناسبة وقوع هذه الآية هنا مناسبة بديعة وهي أن الآيات التي قبلها تكرر فيها التنويه بإبراهيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r4.claim: God places the anticipated taunt before the command to face the Kaaba so the polytheists cannot claim their criticism caused the change; prior allusions to God’s east and west and Jewish and Christian rejection feed the context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p5/r4.anchor: لئلا يكون القرآن الذي فيه الأمر باستقبال الكعبة نازلا بعد مقالة المشركين فيشمخوا بأنوفهم

JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r1.claim: Safīh means ignorant or light-minded; its plural is sufahāʾ. The root suggests lightness: a poor weave is called safīh and winds make something move by lightening it.
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r1.anchor: السفيه: الجاهل، وجمعه السفهاء، وأصله الخفة، والسفيه الخفيف العقل،

JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r2.claim: Turning away and diverting are near-synonyms, as are turning away from something and forbidding it; waliya ʿanhu is opposite waliya ilayhi.
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r2.anchor: ولى عنه وصرفه والنهى عنه نظائر، وولى عنه خلاف ولى إليه،

JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r3.claim: Qibla is the direction faced in prayer, and the Kaʿba is the Muslims’ qibla; the word originally denotes the stance in which one thing faces another, like jalsa.
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r3.anchor: والقبلة: الجهة التي تستقبل في الصلاة، والكعبة قبلة المسلمين، وأصله الحال

JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r4.claim: Yahdī and yadullu are near-synonyms; the original sense of hidāya is indicating or guiding.
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r4.anchor: ويهدي ويدل من النظائر، وأصل الهداية الدلالة.

JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r5.claim: Ṣirāṭ means a straight, even road that continues along one course.
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r5.anchor: والصراط: الطريق المستقيم المستوي المستمر على سنن واحد.

JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r6.claim: One occasion report identifies the critics as Quraysh and Meccans, who said Muḥammad had left his fathers’ qibla and returned to it, so he would return to their religion too.
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r6.anchor: يا محمد رغبت عن قبلة آبائك، ثم رجعت إليها، فلترجعن إلى دينهم، فنزلت الآية، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r7.claim: Another report identifies the foolish critics as Jews.
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: هم اليهود، عن ابن عباس ومجاهد.

JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r8.speaker: السدي
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddī identifies them as hypocrites who made the objection mockingly.
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: المنافقون، عن السدي، وذلك أنهم قالوها استهزاء بالإسلام.

JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r9.claim: Abū Muslim says the critics are the People of the Book, while allowing that polytheists could also be included.
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: هم أهل الكتاب، ويجوز أن يدخل فيه المشركون، عن أبي مسلم.

JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r10.claim: One account includes all groups: hypocrites mocked the switch, Jews said he longed for his birthplace and would have been expected if he stayed with their qibla, and polytheists called him confused.
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: الكل، فالمنافقون قالوا: ما باله توجه قبله زمانا، ثم توجه إلى غيرها،

JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r11.claim: The qibla episode follows the mention of Jewish faults; more broadly, the sequence supplies the Prophet arguments against opponents, first on divine unity, then prophecy, and foretells hurtful criticism to console him and attest to his mission.
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r11.anchor: قيل: لما تقدم ذكر اليهود ومعائبهم ذكر أمرهم في قصة القبلة، وما عابوا به المسلمين،

JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r12.claim: The future tense foretells what ignorant disbelievers will say, presenting their coming objection as consolation and a sign of the Prophet’s truth.
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r12.anchor: فقال تعالى: سيقول أي سوف يقول السفهاء أي الجهال، وهم الكفار،

JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r13.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين، وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r13.claim: The usual interpretation takes the former qibla to be Jerusalem, which Muslims had faced in prayer.
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r13.anchor: يعني بيت المقدس الذي كانوا يتوجهون إليه في صلاتهم، عن جماعة من المفسرين

JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r14.claim: Alternatively, the former qibla may mean the critics’ own directions: Jews and Christians faced east and west, respectively, and faulted Muḥammad for facing the Kaʿba.
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r14.anchor: ويحتمل لفظ الآية أن يراد بقوله: عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها

JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r15.claim: God’s ownership of east and west answers both objections: he determines the qibla and is not restricted to either of the directions opponents recognize.
JISHUMI:v1p618#2/r15.anchor: ولما توجه إلى الكعبة عابوه، وقالوا: كيف يتوجه

JISHUMI:v1p646/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p646/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p646/r1.claim: The statement that God abrogates verses refutes the denial of abrogation, while the qibla question itself shows a community was turned from one qibla to another.
JISHUMI:v1p646/r1.anchor: أما الكتاب فقوله تعالى: (ما ننسخ من آية) يدل على بطلان قوله، وقوله: سيقول السفهاء

JISHUMI:v1p646/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p646/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p646/r2.claim: Reports agree that the qibla was abrogated; Ibn ʿAbbās says facing Jerusalem was the first thing abrogated in the Qur’an.
JISHUMI:v1p646/r2.anchor: وأما الأخبار فتظاهرت بأن القبلة نسخت حتى قال ابن عباس: أول ما نسخ من القرآن التوجه إلى بيت المقدس.

JISHUMI:v1p620/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p620/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p620/r1.claim: One explanation for the criticism is rejection of abrogation.

JISHUMI:v1p620/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p620/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p620/r2.claim: Another report says Jews tried to tempt Muḥammad, asking why he left his qibla and promising to follow him if he returned.
JISHUMI:v1p620/r2.anchor: ارجع إليها نتبعك، وأرادوا فتنته، عن ابن عباس أيضا،

JISHUMI:v1p620/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p620/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p620/r3.claim: Arab polytheists may have said it to make their own religion appear true.
JISHUMI:v1p620/r3.anchor: وقيل: قاله مشركو العرب إيهاما أن الحق ما هم عليه.

JISHUMI:v1p620/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p620/r4.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v1p620/r4.claim: The qibla changed because the relevant benefit changed; Jishumī calls this the stronger explanation.
JISHUMI:v1p620/r4.anchor: لتغير المصلحة عن القاضي، وهو أوجه.

JISHUMI:v1p620/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p620/r5.speaker: أبو علي، وأبو القاسم
JISHUMI:v1p620/r5.claim: Alternatively, the Meccan direction to Jerusalem distinguished Muslims from polytheists, and facing the Kaʿba after migration distinguished them from the Jews of Medina, as in 2:143.
JISHUMI:v1p620/r5.anchor: ليتميزوا عن اليهود، عن أبي علي وأبي القاسم.

JISHUMI:v1p620/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p620/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p620/r6.claim: God’s ownership and creation of east and west show that He controls their direction and can command whichever qibla is most beneficial, refuting the claim that the Holy Land must take priority.
JISHUMI:v1p620/r6.anchor: قل يا محمد لله المشرق والمغرب ملكا وخلقا، وفي وجه الاحتجاج به قولان:

JISHUMI:v1p620/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p620/r7.speaker: الربيع
JISHUMI:v1p620/r7.claim: There is agreement that God made Jerusalem a qibla, but al-Rabīʿ says He gave the Prophet a choice and the Prophet chose it.
JISHUMI:v1p620/r7.anchor: فقيل: إنه تعالى خيره، فاختار بيت المقدس، عن الربيع،

JISHUMI:v1p620/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p620/r8.speaker: ابن عباس، وأكثر المفسرين
JISHUMI:v1p620/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most commentators say facing Jerusalem was imposed on the Prophet rather than chosen.
JISHUMI:v1p620/r8.anchor: وقيل: بل فرض ذلك عليه، عن ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين.

JISHUMI:v1p620/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p620/r9.speaker: ابن عباس، والبراء بن عازب
JISHUMI:v1p620/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib date the qibla change to seventeen months after the Prophet’s arrival in Medina.
JISHUMI:v1p620/r9.anchor: قيل: بعد سبعة عشر شهرا من مقدمه المدينة، عن ابن عباس والبراء بن عازب،

JISHUMI:v1p620/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p620/r10.speaker: أنس بن مالك
JISHUMI:v1p620/r10.claim: Anas ibn Mālik dates the change to nineteen months after arrival in Medina.
JISHUMI:v1p620/r10.anchor: وقيل: بعد تسعة عشر شهرا، عن أنس بن مالك،

JISHUMI:v1p620/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p620/r11.speaker: معاذ
JISHUMI:v1p620/r11.claim: Muʿādh dates the change to thirteen months after arrival in Medina.
JISHUMI:v1p620/r11.anchor: وقيل: بعد ثلاثة عشر شهرا، عن معاذ،

JISHUMI:v1p620/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p620/r12.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v1p620/r12.claim: Qatāda dates the change to eighteen months after arrival in Medina.
JISHUMI:v1p620/r12.anchor: وقيل: بعد ثمانية عشر شهرا عن قتادة

JISHUMI:v1p620/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p620/r13.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p620/r13.claim: The straight path is the religion, or the road leading to Paradise and Paradise itself.
JISHUMI:v1p620/r13.anchor: يهدي من يشاء أي يدله ويرشده إلى صراط مستقيم أي طريق سوي،

JISHUMI:v1p620/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p620/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p620/r14.claim: The verse supports the permissibility of abrogation because the question plainly implies that the community had one qibla before being transferred to another.
JISHUMI:v1p620/r14.anchor: الآية تدل على جواز النسخ؛ لأن قوله: ما ولاهم كالصريح في أنهم كانوا على قبلة،
